translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 226.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十二】　起屠維協洽八月，盡重光作噩五月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 42] Beginning from the eighth month of Tuwéi Xiehe, ending at the fifth month of Chongguang Zuoe—in all a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 42] From the eighth month of the year jǐwèi (779) through the fifth month of the year gēngshēn (780)—a little more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝下大歷十四年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Daizong, the Sagaciously Cultured, Filial, and Martial, the fourteenth year of Dali (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daizong, the Sagaciously Cultured, Filial, and Martial—the fourteenth year of the Dali era (

sentences.zh: 己未，公元七七九年）

translations.literal: jǐwèi, corresponding to the year 779 of the Common Era).
translations.idiomatic: jǐwèi, corresponding to 779 CE).

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，以道州司馬楊炎為門下侍郎，懷州刺史喬琳為御史大夫，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jiachen, Yang Yan, prefectural adjutant of Daozhou, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Qiao Lin, prefect of Huaizhou, was made Censor-in-Chief; both were appointed Junior Chancellors of equal rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jiachen, Yang Yan, adjutant of Daozhou, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Qiao Lin, prefect of Huaizhou, was made Censor-in-Chief; both received the title of Junior Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 上方勵精求治，不次用人，卜相於崔祐甫，祐甫薦炎器業，上亦素聞其名，故自遷謫中用之。

translations.literal: The emperor above was vigorously applying himself to seek good governance, employing men out of turn; he consulted Cui Youfu on appointing a chancellor, and Youfu recommended Yang Yan for his talent and capacity; the emperor had also long heard his name, and therefore used him from among those in exile and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was vigorously striving for good government and promoting men out of turn. When he consulted Cui Youfu about whom to appoint chancellor, Youfu recommended Yang Yan for his talent and ability; the emperor had long heard his name as well, and therefore recalled him from exile and put him in office.

sentences.zh: 琳，太原人，性粗率，喜詼諧，無他長，與張涉善，涉稱其才可大用，上信涉言而用之；

translations.literal: Lin was a man of Taiyuan, coarse and blunt in nature, fond of humor, with no other special merit; he was on good terms with Zhang She, and She praised his talent as fit for great employment; the emperor trusted She’s words and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was a native of Taiyuan, coarse and blunt by nature, fond of wit and banter, with no other special merit. He was friendly with Zhang She, who praised his talent as fit for high office, and the emperor trusted She’s recommendation and appointed him.

sentences.zh: 聞者無不駭愕。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it were without exception startled and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard of it was astonished.

sentences.zh: 代宗之世，吐蕃數遣使求和，而寇盜不息，代宗悉留其使者，前後八輩，有至老死不得歸者；

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Daizong, Tibet repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace, yet raiding and plunder did not cease; Daizong detained all their envoys—eight missions in succession—and some grew old and died without ever returning home.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Daizong’s reign, Tibet sent envoys repeatedly to sue for peace, yet raids never ceased. Daizong detained every envoy—eight missions in all—and some grew old and died without ever returning home.

sentences.zh: 俘獲其人，皆配江、嶺。

translations.literal: Captured Tibetans were all assigned to the Jiang and Ling regions.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners taken from Tibet were all exiled to the Yangtze and Lingnan regions.

sentences.zh: 上欲以德懷之，乙巳，以隨州司馬韋倫為太常少卿，使於吐蕃，悉集其俘五百人，各賜襲衣而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to win them by virtue; on the day yisi, Wei Lun, prefectural adjutant of Suizhou, was made Vice Minister of Imperial Ceremonies and sent to Tibet; all five hundred captives were assembled, each given a suit of clothing, and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor wished to win them over with kindness. On the day yisi, Wei Lun, adjutant of Suizhou, was appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Ceremonies and sent to Tibet; all five hundred captives were gathered, each given a suit of clothing, and released to return home.

sentences.zh: 協律郎沈既濟上選舉議，以為：「選用之法，三科而已：曰德也、才也、勞也。

translations.literal: Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Shen Jiji submitted a memorial on the selection system, stating: “The method of selection has only three categories: namely virtue, talent, and service.”
translations.idiomatic: Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Shen Jiji submitted a memorial on the civil-service selection system, arguing: “The proper criteria for appointment are only three: virtue, talent, and meritorious service.”

sentences.zh: 今選曹皆不及焉；

translations.literal: Today the Selection Bureau reaches none of these.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Selection Bureau pays attention to none of them.

sentences.zh: 考校之法，皆在書判、簿歷、言詞、俯仰而已。

translations.literal: The methods of examination and verification rest solely on written judgments, ledgers and records, speech, and bearing and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: The methods of examination rest solely on written judgments, service records, manner of speech, and deportment.

sentences.zh: 夫安行徐言，非德也；

translations.literal: Now, slow gait and measured speech are not virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Slow gait and measured speech are not virtue.

sentences.zh: 麗藻芳翰，非才也；

translations.literal: Ornate phrasing and elegant brushwork are not talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ornate phrasing and elegant prose are not talent.

sentences.zh: 累資積考，非勞也。

translations.literal: Accumulated seniority and piled-up examinations are not service.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated seniority and piled-up examination scores are not meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 執此以求天下之士，固未盡矣。

translations.literal: To hold to these in seeking the gentlemen of the realm is surely not exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: To rely on these criteria in seeking talent for the empire is plainly inadequate.

sentences.zh: 今人未土著，不可本於鄉閭；

translations.literal: Today people are not rooted in native soil; one cannot rely on village and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: People today are no longer rooted in their native places; one cannot rely on local reputation alone.

sentences.zh: 鑒不獨明，不可專於吏部。

translations.literal: The mirror is not alone bright; one cannot concentrate solely on the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: No single office has a monopoly on clear judgment; one cannot leave everything to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 臣謹詳酌古今，謂五品以上及群司長官，宜令宰臣進敘，吏部、兵部得參議焉。

translations.literal: Your servant has carefully weighed past and present and submits that for officials of the fifth rank and above and chiefs of the various bureaus, the chancellors should be ordered to advance nominations, with the Ministries of Personnel and War permitted to join in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I have carefully weighed past and present practice and submit that for officials of the fifth rank and above and for heads of major offices, the chancellors should advance nominations, with the Ministries of Personnel and War allowed to participate in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 其六品以下或僚佐之屬，許州、府辟用，其牧守、將帥或選用非公，則吏部、兵部得察而舉之，罪其私冒。

translations.literal: For those of the sixth rank and below or the class of aides and assistants, let prefectures and districts be permitted to appoint them; if governors, prefects, or military commanders make selections that are not fair, then the Ministries of Personnel and War may investigate and impeach them, punishing private favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: For officials of the sixth rank and below, or for aides and staff, let prefectures and districts be permitted to appoint them directly. If a governor, prefect, or military commander makes an improper appointment, the Ministries of Personnel and War should investigate and impeach him, punishing private favoritism.

sentences.zh: 不慎舉者，小加譴黜，大正刑典。

translations.literal: Those who are not careful in their recommendations should receive minor censure and demotion, or, in serious cases, punishment under the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Those careless in their recommendations should face minor censure and demotion; in serious cases, punishment under the penal code.

sentences.zh: 責成授任，誰敢不勉！

translations.literal: When responsibility is fixed and office conferred, who would dare not exert himself!
translations.idiomatic: When responsibility is fixed and office conferred, who would dare not do his utmost!

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則賢者不獎而自進，不肖者不抑而自退，眾才咸得而官無不治矣。

translations.literal: If it is thus, then the worthy will advance of themselves without needing reward, the unworthy will withdraw of themselves without needing suppression, all talents will be obtained, and no office will go ungoverned.
translations.idiomatic: If this were done, the worthy would advance without needing encouragement, the unworthy would withdraw without needing suppression, all talent would be put to use, and every office would be well governed.

sentences.zh: 今選法皆擇才於吏部，試職於州郡。

translations.literal: Today the selection law chooses talent at the Ministry of Personnel and tests office in prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present system, talent is selected at the Ministry of Personnel and tested in office at the prefectural level.

sentences.zh: 若才職不稱，紊亂無任，責於刺史，則曰命官出於吏曹，不敢廢也；

translations.literal: If talent and office do not match, and disorder and incompetence prevail, and one holds the prefect accountable, he says the appointed official came from the personnel bureau and he dares not dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: If talent and office do not match and disorder results, and one holds the prefect accountable, he says the appointee came from the Ministry of Personnel and he dares not dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 責於侍郎，則曰量書判、資考而授之，不保其往也；

translations.literal: If one holds the vice minister accountable, he says he measured written judgments and seniority in examinations and conferred the post, and does not guarantee what follows.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds the vice minister accountable, he says he measured written judgments and examination records when making the appointment and cannot be held responsible for what happens afterward.

sentences.zh: 責於令史，則曰按由歷、出入而行之，不知其他也。

translations.literal: If one holds the clerk accountable, he says he proceeded according to dossiers and records of entry and exit and knows nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds the clerk accountable, he says he acted according to the files and service records and knows nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 黎庶徒弊，誰任其咎！

translations.literal: The common people suffer in vain—who bears the blame!
translations.idiomatic: The common people suffer for nothing—who bears the blame!

sentences.zh: 若牧守自用，則罪將焉逃！

translations.literal: If governors and prefects appoint their own men, where can guilt escape!
translations.idiomatic: If governors and prefects appoint their own men, guilt cannot be shifted elsewhere!

sentences.zh: 必州郡之濫，獨換一刺史則革矣。

translations.literal: If there is abuse in prefectures and districts, replacing a single prefect will reform it.
translations.idiomatic: If there is abuse at the prefectural level, replacing a single prefect will cure it.

sentences.zh: 如吏部之濫，雖更其侍郎無益也。

translations.literal: If there is abuse in the Ministry of Personnel, even changing its vice minister is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If there is abuse in the Ministry of Personnel, even replacing its vice minister will do no good.

sentences.zh: 蓋人物浩浩，不可得而知，法使之然，非主司之過。

translations.literal: For talent is vast and boundless and cannot be fully known; the law makes it so—it is not the fault of the chief official.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is vast and cannot be fully known in advance; the system makes this inevitable—it is not the fault of the chief official.

sentences.zh: 今諸道節度、都團練、觀察、租庸等使，自判官、副將以下，皆使自擇，縱其間或有情故，大舉其例，十猶七全。

translations.literal: Today the military governors, grand training commissioners, observation commissioners, and tax commissioners of the various circuits, from adjutants and deputy generals downward, all choose their own men; even if there is sometimes private favor among them, taking the whole by the rule, seven out of ten are sound.
translations.idiomatic: Today the military governors, training commissioners, observation commissioners, and tax commissioners of the various circuits all choose their own subordinates from adjutants and deputy generals downward; even allowing for occasional favoritism, on the whole seven out of ten appointments prove sound.

sentences.zh: 則辟吏之法，已試於今，但未及於州縣耳。

translations.literal: Thus the method of appointing subordinates has already been tested in the present day—it has only not yet reached prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: The method of local appointment has already been tested in practice today—it has simply not yet been extended to the prefectural and county level.

sentences.zh: 利害之理，較然可觀。

translations.literal: The reasoning of benefit and harm is clear enough to be seen by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The balance of advantage and disadvantage is clear enough to see by comparison.

sentences.zh: 曏令諸使僚佐盡受於選曹，則安能鎮方隅之重，理財賦之殷乎！

translations.literal: If formerly all aides of the commissioners had been received from the Selection Bureau, how could they have secured the weight of a frontier region or administered abundant revenues and taxes!
translations.idiomatic: If all these commissioners’ subordinates had to be appointed by the Selection Bureau, how could they have held the weight of a frontier command or administered abundant tax revenues!

sentences.zh: 」既濟，吳人也。

translations.literal: ” Jiji was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jiji was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 初，衡州刺史曹王皋有治行，湖南觀察使辛京杲疾之，陷以法，貶潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cao Wang Gao, prefect of Hengzhou, had a record of good governance; Xin Jinggao, observation commissioner of Hunan, resented him, trapped him by law, and demoted him to prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Cao Gao, prefect of Hengzhou, had a reputation for good governance. Xin Jinggao, observation commissioner of Hunan, resented him, trapped him on a legal pretext, and demoted him to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時楊炎在道州，知其直，及入相，復擢為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Yan was in Daozhou and knew his integrity; when Yan entered the chancellorship, he again promoted Gao to prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was then serving in Daozhou and knew him to be upright; when Yan became chancellor, he had Gao restored as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，皋之遭誣在治，念太妃老，將驚而戚，出則囚服就辨，入則擁笏垂魚，即貶於潮，以遷入賀；

translations.literal: At first, when Gao suffered false accusation while in office, he thought of the Dowager Consort’s age and feared to alarm and grieve her; going out he wore prisoner’s garb to answer the charge, entering he held the tablet and wore the fish pendant; even when demoted to Chaozhou he presented it as a transfer and came in to congratulate her.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao first faced false accusation in office, he thought of the Dowager Consort’s advanced age and feared to alarm or grieve her. When he went out he wore prisoner’s garb to answer the charge; when he came in he held his official tablet and wore his court insignia. Even after his demotion to Chaozhou he presented it to her as a transfer and came in to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 及是，然後跪謝告實。

translations.literal: Only at this time did he kneel, apologize, and tell her the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did he kneel, apologize, and tell her what had really happened.

sentences.zh: 皋，明之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Gao was the great-great-grandson of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 朔方、邠寧節度使李懷光既代郭子儀，邠府宿將史抗、溫儒雅、龐仙鶴、張獻明、李光逸功名素出懷光右，皆怏怏不服。

translations.literal: Li Huai’guang, military governor of Shuofang and Binning, having succeeded Guo Ziyi, the veteran generals of Bin prefecture—Shi Kang, Wen Ruya, Pang Xianhe, Zhang Xianming, and Li Guangyi—whose fame and achievements had always ranked above Huai’guang, were all resentful and unwilling to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Huai’guang succeeded Guo Ziyi as military governor of Shuofang and Binning, the veteran generals of Bin prefecture—Shi Kang, Wen Ruya, Pang Xianhe, Zhang Xianming, and Li Guangyi—whose fame and achievements had always surpassed Huai’guang’s, were all resentful and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 懷光發兵防秋，屯長武城，軍期進退，不時應令。

translations.literal: Huai’guang mobilized troops for autumn defense and encamped at Changwu Fort; on the army’s schedule for advance and withdrawal he did not respond to orders in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Huai’guang mobilized troops for the autumn defense and encamped at Changwu Fort, but failed to advance or withdraw on schedule as ordered.

sentences.zh: 監軍翟文秀勸懷光奏令宿衛，懷光遣之，既離營，使人追捕，誣以它罪，且曰：「黃萯之敗，職爾之由！

translations.literal: Army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu urged Huai’guang to memorialize requesting that they remain on palace guard duty; Huai’guang sent them off, and once they had left camp he had men pursue and seize them, falsely charging other crimes, and saying: “The defeat at Huangfu was your doing!
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu urged Huai’guang to request that they be kept on palace guard duty. Huai’guang sent them off, but once they had left camp he had them pursued and seized on other trumped-up charges, saying: “The defeat at Huangfu was your fault!

sentences.zh: 」盡殺之。

translations.literal: ” He killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: ” and had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲戌，改淮西為淮寧。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jiaxu, Huaixi was renamed Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day jiaxu, the Huaixi circuit was renamed Huaining.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使、同平章事崔寧，在蜀十餘年，恃地險兵強，恣為淫侈，朝廷患之而不能易。

translations.literal: Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan and Junior Chancellor of equal rank, had been in Shu for more than ten years; relying on the region’s rugged terrain and strong troops, he indulged in extravagance at will; the court was troubled by him but could not replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan and Junior Chancellor, had ruled Shu for more than ten years. Relying on the region’s rugged terrain and strong army, he indulged in extravagance at will. The court was troubled by him but could not replace him.

sentences.zh: 至是，入朝，加司空，兼山陵使。

translations.literal: At this time he came to court and was promoted to Minister of Works, concurrently serving as commissioner for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he came to court and was promoted to Minister of Works, with the additional duty of commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 南詔王閣羅鳳卒，子鳳迦異前死，孫異牟尋立。

translations.literal: Geluo Feng, king of Nanzhao, died; his son Fengjiayi had died earlier, and his grandson Yimouxun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Geluo Feng, king of Nanzhao, died. His son Fengjiayi had died earlier, and his grandson Yimouxun succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉朔，吐蕃與南詔合兵十萬，三道入寇，一出茂州，一出扶、文，一出黎、雅，曰：「吾欲取蜀以為東府。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon of the day dingyou, Tibet and Nanzhao united an army of one hundred thousand and invaded by three routes—one out of Maozhou, one out of Fu and Wen, one out of Li and Ya—saying: “We wish to take Shu and make it our eastern capital.”
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon of the day dingyou, Tibet and Nanzhao united a force of one hundred thousand men and invaded by three routes—one through Maozhou, one through Fu and Wen, and one through Li and Ya—declaring: “We intend to take Shu and make it our eastern capital.”

sentences.zh: 」崔寧在京師，所留諸將不能御，虜連陷州、縣，刺史棄城走，士民竄匿山谷。

translations.literal: Cui Ning was in the capital; the generals he had left behind could not resist; the invaders successively captured prefectures and districts; prefects abandoned their cities and fled; soldiers and common people hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning was in the capital, and the generals he had left behind could not hold them off. The invaders captured prefecture after prefecture; prefects abandoned their cities and fled; soldiers and civilians hid in the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 上憂之，趣寧歸鎮。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled and urged Ning to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and urged Ning to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 寧已辭，楊炎言於上曰：「蜀地富饒，寧據有之，朝廷失其外府，十四年矣。

translations.literal: Ning had already taken leave when Yang Yan said to the emperor: “The land of Shu is rich; Ning holds it, and the court has lost its outer capital for fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had already taken his leave when Yang Yan said to the emperor: “Shu is a rich region, and Ning has held it while the court has lost its outer capital for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 寧雖入朝，全師尚守其後，貢賦不入，與無蜀同。

translations.literal: Although Ning has come to court, his full army still guards behind him; tribute and taxes do not enter—it is the same as having no Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ning has come to court, his entire army still guards Shu behind him; tribute and taxes do not reach the capital—it is as if we had no Shu at all.

sentences.zh: 且寧本與諸將等夷，因亂得位，威令不行。

translations.literal: Moreover, Ning was originally the equal of the other generals and gained his position through disorder; his authority and orders do not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Ning was originally no better than the other generals and gained his position only through the disorders of the times; his authority does not truly command obedience.

sentences.zh: 今雖遣之，必恐無功；

translations.literal: Even if we send him now, I fear he will surely achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we send him back now, I fear he will accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 若其有功，則義不可奪。

translations.literal: If he should have merit, then by right he cannot be removed.
translations.idiomatic: If he should succeed, we could not remove him by right.

sentences.zh: 是蜀地敗固失之，勝亦不得也。

translations.literal: Thus if Shu is defeated we lose it in any case; if victorious we still cannot gain it.
translations.idiomatic: In defeat we lose Shu in any case; in victory we still cannot regain control of it.

sentences.zh: 願陛下熟察。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然則奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Then what is to be done?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Then what should we do?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「請留寧，發朱泚所領范陽戍兵數千人，雜禁兵往擊之，何憂不克！

translations.literal: He replied: “I ask that Ning be kept here and that several thousand garrison troops of Fanyang under Zhu Ci’s command be sent, mixed with palace guards, to strike them—why worry that they will not be defeated!”
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, “Keep Ning here and send several thousand Fanyang garrison troops under Zhu Ci’s command, mixed with palace guards, to strike the invaders—why should we fear they cannot be defeated!”

sentences.zh: 因而得內親兵於其腹中，蜀將必不敢動，然後更授他帥，使千里沃壤復為國有，是因小害而收大利也。

translations.literal: Thereby we can place imperial guards within Shu itself; the Shu generals will surely not dare move; then we can appoint another commander and make a thousand li of fertile land state property again—this is to accept a small harm and reap a great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: We can thereby station imperial troops inside Shu itself; the Shu generals will not dare move against us. Then we can appoint another commander and restore a thousand li of fertile land to the state—accepting a small cost for a great gain.”

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Good.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Good.”

sentences.zh: 」遂留寧。

translations.literal: Ning was therefore kept.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was therefore kept at court.

sentences.zh: 初，馬璘忌涇原都知兵馬使李晟功名，遣入宿衛，為右神策都將。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Lin had resented the fame and achievement of Li Sheng, chief commander of troops and horses of Jingyuan, and sent him to palace guard duty as a general of the Right Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ma Lin had resented Li Sheng, chief commander of Jingyuan, for his fame and achievements, and had him transferred to palace guard duty as a general of the Right Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 上發禁兵四千人，使晟將之，發邠、隴、范陽兵五千，使金吾大將軍安邑曲環將之，以救蜀。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched four thousand palace guards for Li Sheng to command, and five thousand troops from Bin, Long, and Fanyang for Qu Huan of Anyi, Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard, to command, to rescue Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched four thousand palace guards under Li Sheng’s command, and five thousand troops from Bin, Long, and Fanyang under Qu Huan of Anyi, Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard, to relieve Shu.

sentences.zh: 東川出軍，自江油趣白壩，與山南兵合擊吐蕃、南詔，破之。

translations.literal: Dongchuan sent out troops from Jiangyou toward Baiba and, joining with Shannan troops, struck Tibet and Nanzhao and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dongchuan sent troops from Jiangyou toward Baiba and, joining forces with the Shannan army, attacked Tibet and Nanzhao and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 范陽兵追及於七盤，又破之，遂克維、茂二州。

translations.literal: Fanyang troops overtook them at Qipan and defeated them again, then captured the two prefectures of Wei and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang troops overtook them at Qipan and defeated them again, then recaptured the prefectures of Wei and Mao.

sentences.zh: 李晟追擊於大度河外，又破之。

translations.literal: Li Sheng pursued beyond the Dadu River and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng pursued them beyond the Dadu River and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃、南詔饑寒隕於崖谷死者八九萬人。

translations.literal: Tibetans and Nanzhao men who perished from hunger and cold in cliff valleys numbered eighty or ninety thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty or ninety thousand Tibetans and Nanzhao soldiers died of hunger and cold in the mountain ravines.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃悔怒，殺誘導使之來者。

translations.literal: Tibet, in regret and rage, killed those who had come to lure and guide them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet, furious and regretful, executed those who had urged them to invade.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋懼，築苴咩城，延袤十五里，徙居之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun was afraid, built Jumie City extending fifteen li, and moved his residence there.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun was frightened, built Jumie City fifteen li in extent, and moved his capital there.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃封之為日東王。

translations.literal: Tibet enfeoffed him as King of the Eastern Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet enfeoffed him as King of the Eastern Sun.

sentences.zh: 上用法嚴，百官震悚。

translations.literal: The emperor applied the law strictly, and the hundred officials were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enforced the law strictly, and the officials were all shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 以山陵近，禁人屠宰；

translations.literal: Because the imperial tomb was near, slaughter by the people was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Because the imperial tomb work was approaching, the slaughter of livestock was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀之隸人潛殺羊，載以入城，右金吾將軍裴諝奏之。

translations.literal: A servant of Guo Ziyi secretly slaughtered a sheep and carried it into the city; Pei Xu, general of the Right Golden Crow Guard, memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: A servant of Guo Ziyi secretly slaughtered a sheep and brought it into the city; Pei Xu, general of the Right Golden Crow Guard, reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 或謂諝曰：「郭公有社稷大功，君獨不為之地乎？

translations.literal: Someone said to Xu: “Duke Guo has great merit for the altars of state—will you alone not make allowance for him?”
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Xu, “Duke Guo has rendered great service to the state—will you not make allowance for him?”

sentences.zh: 」諝曰：「此乃吾所以為之地也。

translations.literal: Xu said: “This is precisely how I make allowance for him.”
translations.idiomatic: Xu replied, “This is precisely how I am making allowance for him.”

sentences.zh: 郭公勳高望重，上新即位，以為群臣附之者眾，吾故發其小過，以明郭公威權不足畏也。

translations.literal: Duke Guo’s merit is high and his prestige heavy; the emperor has newly ascended the throne and believes many ministers attach themselves to Guo; I therefore expose his small fault to make clear that Duke Guo’s authority and power are not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Guo’s merit is great and his prestige weighty; the new emperor fears that many ministers are attached to him. I therefore expose this small fault to show that Duke Guo’s power is not to be feared.

sentences.zh: 如此，上尊天子，下安大臣，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Thus the sovereign above is honored and the great ministers below are secured—is this not acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: In this way the emperor’s authority is upheld above and the great ministers are reassured below—is that not the right course!”

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬睿文孝武皇帝於元陵；

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, the Sagaciously Cultured, Filial, and Martial Emperor was buried at Yuan Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, the Sagaciously Cultured, Filial, and Martial Emperor was buried at Yuan Tomb;

sentences.zh: 廟號代宗。

translations.literal: His temple name was Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: his temple name was Daizong.

sentences.zh: 將發引，上送之，見轀輬車不當馳道，稍指丁未之間，問其故，有司對曰：「陛下本命在午，不敢沖也。

translations.literal: When the procession was about to set out, the emperor escorted it and saw that the imperial hearse was not on the imperial roadway but pointed slightly toward the dingwei interval; he asked the reason, and the responsible officials replied: “Your Majesty’s natal destiny lies in the wu hour; we dared not clash with it.”
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession was about to depart, the emperor escorted it and noticed that the imperial hearse was not on the imperial roadway but angled slightly toward the dingwei direction. He asked why, and the officials in charge replied, “Your Majesty’s natal destiny lies in the wu hour; we dared not let the procession clash with it.”

sentences.zh: 」上哭曰：「安有枉靈駕而謀身利乎！

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: “How can there be bending the spirit carriage to seek personal advantage!”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, “How can we bend the imperial procession to seek personal advantage!”

sentences.zh: 」命改轅直午而行。

translations.literal: He ordered the shafts changed to go straight through the wu direction.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the shafts turned so the procession would go straight through the wu direction.

sentences.zh: 肅宗、代宗皆喜陰陽鬼神，事無大小，必謀之卜祝，故王嶼、黎幹以左道得進。

translations.literal: Emperors Suzong and Daizong both delighted in yin-yang and ghosts and spirits; in matters large and small they invariably consulted diviners and prayer masters, and therefore Wang Yu and Li Gan advanced by heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Suzong and Daizong had both been devoted to yin-yang lore and spirits; on matters large and small they invariably consulted diviners and prayer masters, which was how Wang Yu and Li Gan rose by heterodox means.

sentences.zh: 上雅不之信，山陵但取七月之期，事集而發，不復擇日。

translations.literal: The present emperor by nature did not believe in these things; for the tomb he took only the seventh-month deadline, setting out when matters were ready, and did not again choose a day.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor did not believe in such things. For the tomb he took only the seventh-month deadline, setting out when preparations were complete, and did not again choose an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁丑，以晉州刺史韓滉為蘇州刺史、浙江東、西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day dingchou, Han Huang, prefect of Jinzou, was made prefect of Suzhou and observation commissioner of eastern and western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day dingchou, Han Huang, prefect of Jinzhou, was appointed prefect of Suzhou and observation commissioner of eastern and western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 喬琳衰老耳聵，上或時訪問，應對失次，所謀議復疏闊。

translations.literal: Qiao Lin was aged and deaf; when the emperor sometimes consulted him, his replies were out of order and his counsel was again loose and wide of the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin was aged and hard of hearing. When the emperor occasionally consulted him, his replies were confused and his counsel vague and impractical.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以琳為工部尚書，罷政事。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Lin was made Minister of Works and removed from affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, Lin was appointed Minister of Works and dismissed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 上由是疏張涉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby grew distant from Zhang She.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereby grew cool toward Zhang She.

sentences.zh: 楊炎既留崔寧，二人由是交惡。

translations.literal: Yang Yan having kept Cui Ning, the two thereby became mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Yan had kept Cui Ning at court, the two men became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 炎托以北邊須大臣鎮撫，癸巳，以京畿觀察使崔寧為單于、鎮北大都護、朔方節度使，鎮坊州。

translations.literal: Yan pleaded that the northern frontier required a great minister to pacify and soothe it; on the day guisi, Cui Ning, observation commissioner of the capital region, was made Protector General of Chanyu, Grand Protector of the North, and military governor of Shuofang, stationed at Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued that the northern frontier required a senior minister to pacify it. On the day guisi, Cui Ning, observation commissioner of the capital region, was appointed Protector General of Chanyu, Grand Protector of the North, and military governor of Shuofang, with his headquarters at Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以荊南節度使張延賞為西川節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang, military governor of Jingnan, was made military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang, military governor of Jingnan, was appointed military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 又以靈鹽節度都虞侯醴泉杜希全知靈、鹽州留後；

translations.literal: Du Xiquan of Liquan, chief adjutant of the Ling-Salt command, was also made acting prefect of Ling and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan of Liquan, chief adjutant of the Ling-Salt command, was also made acting prefect of Ling and Yan prefectures;

sentences.zh: 代州刺史張光晟知單于、振武等城、綏、銀、麟、勝州留後；

translations.literal: Zhang Guangsheng, prefect of Daizhou, was made acting prefect of the Chanyu, Zhenwu, and other fortresses and of Sui, Yin, Lin, and Sheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsheng, prefect of Daizhou, was made acting prefect of the Chanyu and Zhenwu garrisons and of Sui, Yin, Lin, and Sheng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 延州刺史李建徽知鄜、坊、丹州留後。

translations.literal: Li Jianhui, prefect of Yanzhou, was made acting prefect of Fu, Fang, and Dan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianhui, prefect of Yanzhou, was made acting prefect of Fu, Fang, and Dan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時寧既出鎮，不當更置留後，炎欲奪寧權，且窺其所為，令三人皆得自奏事，仍諷之使伺寧過失。

translations.literal: At the time Ning had already gone out to his command and there should not have been further appointment of acting prefects; Yan wished to strip Ning of power and also spy on his conduct, ordering the three men all to memorialize the throne directly on their own and hinting to them to watch for Ning's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had already taken up his command and should no longer have had acting prefects appointed over him. Yang Yan wished to strip Ning of power and spy on his conduct, so he allowed all three men to memorialize the throne directly and hinted that they should watch for Ning's faults.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，立宣王誦為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day yimao, Prince Xuan Song was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day yimao, Prince Xuan Song was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 舊制，天下金帛皆貯於左藏，太府四時上其數，比部覆其出入。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the empire's gold and silk were all stored in the Left Treasury; the Court of the Imperial Treasury reported the figures each season, and the Ministry of Revenue audited receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, the empire's gold and silk were stored in the Left Treasury; the Court of the Imperial Treasury reported the figures each season, and the Ministry of Revenue audited receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 及第五琦為度支、鹽鐵使，時京師多豪將，求取無節，琦不能制，乃奏盡貯於大盈內庫，使宦官掌之，天子亦以取給為便，故久不出。

translations.literal: When Diwu Qi became commissioner of revenue and salt and iron, at the time the capital had many powerful generals who sought funds without restraint and Qi could not control them; he therefore memorialized that everything be stored in the Great Abundance inner treasury, with eunuchs in charge; the Son of Heaven also found it convenient for his own supplies, and therefore it was long not released.
translations.idiomatic: When Diwu Qi became commissioner of revenue and of salt and iron, many powerful generals in the capital demanded funds without restraint, and Qi could not control them. He therefore proposed storing all revenues in the Great Abundance inner treasury under eunuch management. The emperor also found it convenient for his personal expenses, and the funds were long kept from the regular administration.

sentences.zh: 由是以天下公賦為人君私藏，有司不復得窺其多少，校其贏縮，殆二十年。

translations.literal: Thereby the public taxes of the realm became the monarch's private hoard; responsible officials could no longer see how much there was or check surplus and deficit—for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the public revenues of the realm became the emperor's private hoard. Responsible officials could no longer see how much was held or check surplus and deficit—for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 宦官領其事者三百餘員，皆蠶食其中，蟠結根據，牢不可動。

translations.literal: Eunuchs in charge of the matter numbered more than three hundred, all gnawing at it from within, coiling roots and bases, firmly immovable.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred eunuchs managed these funds, all feeding on them from within and entrenching themselves so firmly that they could not be dislodged.

sentences.zh: 楊炎頓首於上前曰：「財賦者，國之大本，生民之命，重輕安危，靡不由之，是以前世皆使重臣掌其事，猶或耗亂不集。

translations.literal: Yang Yan kowtowed before the emperor and said: "Revenue and taxes are the great foundation of the state and the life of the people; weighty or light, safe or perilous—all depend on them. Therefore past ages all had weighty ministers manage the matter, yet there was still waste, disorder, and failure to gather funds.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan kowtowed before the emperor and said, "Revenue and taxation are the great foundation of the state and the livelihood of the people. The state's strength and security all depend on them. Past ages therefore entrusted weighty ministers with this duty, yet waste and disorder still occurred.

sentences.zh: 今獨使中人出入盈虛，大臣皆不得知，政之蠹敝，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: Today only palace attendants control surplus and deficit, and great ministers may not know—of the corruption and decay of government, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Today only eunuchs control the surplus and deficit, and great ministers are kept in ignorance. No corruption in government exceeds this.

sentences.zh: 請出之以歸有司。

translations.literal: I ask that it be brought out and returned to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these funds be returned to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 度宮中歲用幾何，量數奉入，不敢有乏。

translations.literal: Estimate how much the palace uses in a year, measure the amount to be delivered in, and there will be no fear of shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Estimate the palace's annual needs, deliver that amount, and there will be no shortage.

sentences.zh: 如此，然後可以為政。

translations.literal: Only thus can government be conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can government be properly conducted.

sentences.zh: 」上即日下詔：「凡財賦皆歸左藏，一用舊式，歲於數中擇精好者三、五千匹，進入大盈。

translations.literal: The emperor that same day issued an edict: "All revenue and taxes shall return to the Left Treasury and follow the old forms entirely; each year from the total three to five thousand bolts of the finest quality shall be presented to the Great Abundance."
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor issued an edict: "All revenues shall return to the Left Treasury under the old system. Each year three to five thousand bolts of the finest quality shall be presented to the Great Abundance treasury."

sentences.zh: 」炎以片言移人主意，議者稱之。

translations.literal: Yan with a few words shifted the ruler's intent, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had shifted the emperor's mind with a few words, and commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 丙寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month bingyin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month bingyin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 湖南賊帥王國良阻山為盜，上遣都官員外郎關播招撫之。

translations.literal: Wang Guoliang, bandit chief of Hunan, blocked the mountains and acted as a robber; the emperor sent Guan Bo, vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, to win him over by appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guoliang, a bandit leader in Hunan, held the mountains and plundered the countryside. The emperor sent Guan Bo, vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, to win him over by negotiation.

sentences.zh: 辭行，上問以為政之要，對曰：「為政之本，必求有道賢人與之為理。

translations.literal: When he took leave to depart, the emperor asked him about the essentials of governing; he replied: "The root of governing is surely to seek worthy men of the Way and govern with them."
translations.idiomatic: As he took his leave, the emperor asked him about the essentials of good government. He replied, "The foundation of government is to find worthy men of principle and govern with them."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕比以下詔求賢，又遣使臣廣加搜訪，庶幾可以為理乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have lately issued edicts seeking the worthy and also sent envoys to search broadly—might this perhaps suffice for governing!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have lately issued edicts seeking the worthy and sent envoys to search broadly—might that not suffice for good government!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「下詔所求及使者所薦，惟得文詞干進之士耳，安有有道賢人肯隨牒舉選乎！

translations.literal: He replied: "Those sought by edict and recommended by envoys are only men who advance by literary polish—how could there be worthy men of the Way willing to follow documents and enter selection!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Those sought by edict and recommended by envoys are only men who advance through literary polish. How could worthy men of principle be willing to enter the examination system!"

sentences.zh: 」上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫有疾，上令肩輿入中書，或休假在第，大事令中使咨決。

translations.literal: Cui Youfu was ill; the emperor had him carried by sedan chair into the Secretariat, or on leave at his residence; on great matters he had palace envoys consult and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu was ill. The emperor had him carried by sedan chair to the Secretariat, or allowed him to rest at home on leave; on important matters palace envoys were sent to consult him.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武孝文皇帝一（

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, the Divinely Martial and Filially Cultured, Part One (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, the Divinely Martial and Filially Cultured—Part One (

sentences.zh: 庚申，公元七八零年）

translations.literal: gēngshēn, corresponding to the year 780 of the Common Era).
translations.idiomatic: gēngshēn, corresponding to 780 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁卯朔，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day dingmao, the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day dingmao, the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 群臣上尊號曰聖神文武皇帝；

translations.literal: The ministers advanced the honorific title Sagely, Divine, Civil, and Martial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers advanced the honorific title Sagely, Divine, Civil, and Martial Emperor;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: There was an amnesty for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and an amnesty was proclaimed for the realm.

sentences.zh: 始用楊炎議，命黜陟使與觀察使、刺史「約百姓丁產，定等級，作兩稅法。

translations.literal: For the first time Yang Yan's proposal was used, ordering promotion-and-demotion commissioners with observation commissioners and prefects to "assess the households and property of the people, fix grades, and institute the two-tax law.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Yan's proposal for the first time, promotion-and-demotion commissioners, observation commissioners, and prefects were ordered to "assess the households and property of the people, fix tax grades, and institute the two-tax law.

sentences.zh: 比來新舊征科色目，一切罷之；

translations.literal: All old and new categories of levies and collections hitherto are entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All old and new categories of levies hitherto imposed are entirely abolished;

sentences.zh: 二稅外輒率一錢者，以枉法論。

translations.literal: Whoever beyond the two taxes collects even one cash shall be judged under the law for perverting the law.
translations.idiomatic: whoever beyond the two taxes collects even one cash shall be punished for perverting the law."

sentences.zh: 」唐初，賦斂之法曰租、庸、調，有田則有租，有身則有庸，有戶則有調。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, the method of levies was called rent, corvée, and allocation: where there was land there was rent, where there was a person there was corvée, where there was a household there was allocation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tang dynasty, the tax system consisted of rent, corvée, and allocation: landholders paid rent, adult males paid corvée labor, and households paid the allocation tax.

sentences.zh: 玄宗之末，版籍浸壞，多非其實。

translations.literal: By the end of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, household registers were gradually ruined and largely did not reflect reality.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, household registers had fallen into disrepair and no longer reflected reality.

sentences.zh: 及至德兵起，所在賦斂，迫趣取辦，無復常准。

translations.literal: When the Zhide armies rose, levies everywhere were urgently pressed and collected without fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion of the Zhide era broke out, levies were urgently pressed everywhere without fixed standards.

sentences.zh: 賦斂之司增數而莫相統攝，各隨意增科，自立色目，新故相仍，不知紀極。

translations.literal: The offices of levy multiplied in number without mutual oversight; each at will added categories, established its own items, new and old succeeding one another without limit or end.
translations.idiomatic: Tax offices multiplied without central oversight; each added levies at will, invented new categories, and old and new taxes piled on without end.

sentences.zh: 民富者丁多，率為官、為僧以免課役，而貧者丁多，無所伏匿，故上戶優而下戶勞。

translations.literal: Among the people, the rich with many adult males mostly became officials or monks to escape levies and corvée, while the poor with many adult males had nowhere to hide; thus upper households were favored and lower households bore the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families with many adult males mostly became officials or monks to escape taxation, while poor families with many adult males had nowhere to hide. Upper households were favored and lower households bore the burden.

sentences.zh: 吏因緣蠶食，民旬輸月送，不勝困弊，率皆逃徙為浮戶，其土著百無四五。

translations.literal: Officials exploited opportunities to gnaw away; the people paid every ten days and delivered every month, unable to bear the distress; mostly they fled and became floating households; of those rooted in place, not four or five in a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: Officials exploited every opportunity to extort them. The people paid taxes every ten days and every month until they could bear no more; most fled and became unregistered "floating" households. Of those who remained rooted in place, scarcely four or five in a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 至是，炎建議作兩稅法，先計州縣每歲所應費用及上供之數而賦於人，量出以制入。

translations.literal: At this point Yan proposed the two-tax law: first calculate each prefecture and district's annual necessary expenses and the amount for tribute to the center, then levy on the people—measuring outgo to fix income.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Yan proposed the two-tax law: first calculate each prefecture and county's annual expenses and tribute to the center, then levy taxes on the people—fixing revenue according to expenditure.

sentences.zh: 戶無主、客，以見居為簿；

translations.literal: Households were without distinction of native or sojourner; registration was by present residence.
translations.idiomatic: Households were no longer classified as native or sojourner; registration was based on present residence.

sentences.zh: 人無丁、中，以貧富為差；

translations.literal: Persons were without distinction of adult male or youth; grades were by wealth and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Persons were no longer classified by adult male or youth; tax grades were based on wealth.

sentences.zh: 為行商者，在所州縣稅三十之一，使與居者均，無僥利。

translations.literal: Traveling merchants were taxed one-thirtieth in the prefecture or district where they were, making them equal with residents, without opportunistic gain.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling merchants were taxed one-thirtieth in whatever prefecture or county they were in, equalizing their burden with residents and closing loopholes.

sentences.zh: 居人之稅，秋、夏兩征之。

translations.literal: Tax on residents was collected twice, in autumn and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on residents were collected twice a year, in summer and autumn.

sentences.zh: 其租、庸、調雜徭悉省，皆總統於度支。

translations.literal: Rent, corvée, allocation, and miscellaneous corvées were all abolished and unified under the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Rent, corvée, allocation, and miscellaneous labor levies were all abolished and unified under the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上用其言，因赦令行之。

translations.literal: The emperor used his words and implemented them through the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal and implemented it through the amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 初，左僕射劉晏為吏部尚書，楊炎為侍郎，不相悅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Yan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was Minister of Personnel and Yang Yan was vice minister; they were not pleased with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Yan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, had served as Minister of Personnel with Yang Yan as his vice minister; the two disliked each other.

sentences.zh: 元載之死，晏有力焉。

translations.literal: In Yuan Zai's death, Yan had exerted force therein.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan had played a major role in bringing about Yuan Zai's downfall.

sentences.zh: 及上即位，晏久典利權，眾頗疾之，多上言轉運使可罷；

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Yan had long controlled financial power; many resented him and often memorialized that the transport commissioner could be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor ascended the throne, Yan had long controlled financial power. Many resented him, and memorials frequently urged abolishing the transport commissioner post.

sentences.zh: 又有風言晏嘗密表勸代宗立獨孤妃為皇后者。

translations.literal: There was also rumor that Yan had once secretly memorialized urging Emperor Daizong to establish Consort Dugu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: There was also rumor that Yan had once secretly urged Emperor Daizong to make Consort Dugu empress.

sentences.zh: 楊炎為宰相，欲為元載報仇，因為上流涕言：「晏與黎幹、劉忠翼同謀，臣為宰相不能討，罪當萬死！

translations.literal: Yang Yan as chancellor wished to avenge Yuan Zai and therefore said to the emperor with streaming tears: "Yan plotted together with Li Gan and Liu Zhongyi; I as chancellor could not punish them—my crime deserves ten thousand deaths!"
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Yang Yan wished to avenge Yuan Zai. He said to the emperor with streaming tears, "Yan plotted with Li Gan and Liu Zhongyi. As chancellor I could not punish them—my crime deserves death ten thousand times over!"

sentences.zh: 」崔祐甫言：「茲事暖昧，陛下已曠然大赦，不當復究尋虛語。

translations.literal: Cui Youfu said: "This matter is obscure; Your Majesty has already proclaimed a broad amnesty and should not again pursue empty words."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu said, "This matter is obscure. Your Majesty has already proclaimed a broad amnesty and should not pursue empty rumors."

sentences.zh: 」炎乃建言：「尚書省，國政之本，比置諸使，分奪其權，今宜復舊。

translations.literal: Yan then proposed: "The Secretariat is the root of state affairs; lately various commissioners were established, dividing and seizing its power; now the old system should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Yan then proposed, "The Secretariat is the foundation of state affairs. Lately various commissioners have been established that divided its authority. The old system should be restored."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔天下錢穀皆歸金部、倉部，罷晏轉運、租庸、青苗、鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, an edict ordered that money and grain throughout the realm return to the Gold and Granary bureaus and abolished Yan's posts as transport, rent-and-corvée, green-sprout, salt-and-iron, and other commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, an edict ordered that revenues throughout the realm return to the Gold and Granary bureaus and abolished Yan's posts as transport, rent-and-corvée, green-sprout, salt-and-iron, and other commissioners.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙申朔，命黜陟使十一人分巡天下。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the new moon of the day bingshen, eleven promotion-and-demotion commissioners were ordered to tour the realm in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of the day bingshen, eleven promotion-and-demotion commissioners were dispatched to tour the realm.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏博節度使田悅事朝廷猶恭順，河北黜陟使洪經綸，不曉時務，聞悅軍七萬人，符下，罷其四萬，令還農。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tian Yue, military governor of Weibo, still served the court with respect and compliance; Hong Jinglun, promotion-and-demotion commissioner of Hebei, did not understand the affairs of the time; hearing that Yue's army was seventy thousand, he issued a document dismissing forty thousand and ordering them back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tian Yue, military governor of Weibo, had still served the court respectfully. Hong Jinglun, the Hebei promotion-and-demotion commissioner, did not understand the times. Learning that Yue's army numbered seventy thousand men, he issued an order dismissing forty thousand and sending them back to farming.

sentences.zh: 悅陽順命，如符罷之。

translations.literal: Yue outwardly obeyed the order and dismissed them as the document directed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue outwardly obeyed and dismissed them as ordered.

sentences.zh: 既而集應罷者，激怒之曰：「汝曹久在軍中，有父母妻子，今一旦為黜陟使所罷，將何資以自衣食乎！

translations.literal: Then he assembled those who should have been dismissed and incited them, saying: "You have long been in the army with parents, wives, and children; now in a single day you are dismissed by the promotion-and-demotion commissioner—what will you rely on for food and clothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he assembled the men who were to be dismissed and incited them, saying, "You have long served in the army with parents, wives, and children. Now in a single day you are dismissed by the promotion-and-demotion commissioner—how will you feed and clothe yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 」眾大哭。

translations.literal: The crowd wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The men wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 悅乃出家財以賜之，使各還部伍。

translations.literal: Yue then distributed his family wealth to give them gifts and had each return to his unit.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then distributed his family wealth among them as gifts and had each man return to his unit.

sentences.zh: 於是軍士皆德悅而怨朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers all were grateful to Yue and resentful of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the soldiers were grateful to Yue and resentful of the court.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫以疾，多不視事。

translations.literal: Cui Youfu, because of illness, often did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness, Cui Youfu often did not attend to affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 楊炎獨任大政，專以復恩仇為事，奏用元載遺策城原州，又欲發兩京、關內丁夫浚豐州陵陽渠，以興屯田。

translations.literal: Yang Yan alone bore the great administration, devoting himself solely to settling favors and enmities; he memorialized to use Yuan Zai's leftover plan to fortify Yuanzhou, and also wished to mobilize corvée laborers from the two capitals and Guannei to dredge the Lingyang Canal at Fengzhou to establish military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan alone bore the great administration, devoting himself chiefly to settling scores. He memorialized to carry out Yuan Zai's leftover plan to fortify Yuanzhou and also proposed mobilizing corvée laborers from the two capitals and Guannei to dredge the Lingyang Canal at Fengzhou to establish military colonies.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使詣涇原節度使段秀實，訪以利害，秀實以為：「今邊備尚虛，未宜興事以召寇。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to Duan Xiushi, military governor of Jingyuan, to inquire about benefit and harm; Xiushi held that: "Now frontier defenses are still weak; it is not fitting to undertake projects that will summon invaders."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to Duan Xiushi, military governor of Jingyuan, to inquire about the plan's merits. Xiushi replied, "Frontier defenses are still weak. It is not fitting to undertake projects that will provoke invasion."

sentences.zh: 」炎怒，以為沮已，征秀實為司農卿。

translations.literal: Yan was angry, believing Xiushi was obstructing him, and summoned Xiushi as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was furious, believing Xiushi was obstructing him, and recalled him to court as Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 丁未，邠寧節度使李懷光兼四鎮、北庭行營、涇原節度使，使移軍原州，以四鎮、北庭留後劉文喜為別駕。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Li Huai'guang, military governor of Binning, was additionally made military governor of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court expedition and of Jingyuan, ordered to move his army to Yuanzhou, with Liu Wenxi, acting prefect of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court, as vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei, Li Huai'guang, military governor of Binning, was additionally appointed military governor of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court expedition and of Jingyuan, and ordered to move his army to Yuanzhou. Liu Wenxi, acting prefect of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court, was made vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹嚴郢奏：「案朔方五城，舊屯沃饒之地，自喪亂以來，人功不及，因致荒廢，十不耕一。

translations.literal: Yan Yi, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, memorialized: "Examining the five cities of Shuofang, they were formerly garrisoned on fertile and rich land; since the disorders, human labor has not reached them, and they have fallen into waste—not one in ten is cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yi, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, memorialized, "The five cities of Shuofang were formerly garrisoned on fertile land. Since the disorders, labor has not reached them and they have fallen into ruin—not one in ten fields is cultivated.

sentences.zh: 若力可墾辟，不俟浚渠。

translations.literal: If strength can reclaim and open land, there is no need to wait for dredging canals.
translations.idiomatic: If labor is available, the land can be reclaimed without dredging canals.

sentences.zh: 今發兩京、關輔人於豐州浚渠營田，計所得不補所費，而關輔之人不免流散，是虛畿甸而無益軍儲也。

translations.literal: Now to mobilize people from the two capitals and Guanfu to Fengzhou to dredge canals and establish colonies—the yield will not repay the cost, and the people of Guanfu cannot escape dispersal; this is to empty the capital region without benefiting military stores.
translations.idiomatic: To mobilize people from the two capitals and Guanfu to Fengzhou to dredge canals and establish colonies—the yield will not repay the cost, and the people of Guanfu will be driven to flee. This would empty the capital region without benefiting military stores."

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 既而陵陽渠竟不成，棄之。

translations.literal: In the end the Lingyang Canal was not completed and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the Lingyang Canal project was abandoned unfinished.

sentences.zh: 上用楊炎之言，托以奏事不實，己酉，貶劉晏為忠州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor used Yang Yan's words, pleading that his memorials were not factual; on the day jiyou, Liu Yan was demoted to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Yan's advice, on the pretext that Yan's memorials were untruthful, the emperor on the day jiyou demoted Liu Yan to prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以澤潞留後李抱真為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Li Baozhen, acting prefect of Zelu, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, Li Baozhen, acting prefect of Zelu, was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 楊炎欲城原州以復秦、原，命李懷光居前督作，朱泚、崔寧各將萬人翼其後。

translations.literal: Yang Yan wished to fortify Yuanzhou to recover Qin and Yuan, ordering Li Huai'guang to go forward and supervise construction, with Zhu Ci and Cui Ning each commanding ten thousand men to flank behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan wished to fortify Yuanzhou to recover Qin and Yuan prefectures. He ordered Li Huai'guang to go forward and supervise construction, with Zhu Ci and Cui Ning each commanding ten thousand men to support him from the rear.

sentences.zh: 詔下涇州為城具，涇之將士怒曰：「吾屬為國家西門之屏，十餘年矣。

translations.literal: When the edict reached Jingzhou to prepare fortification materials, the generals and soldiers of Jing were angry and said: "We have been the screen of the state's western gate for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached Jingzhou ordering preparations for fortification, the soldiers of Jing were furious. They said, "We have been the shield of the empire's western gate for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 始居邠州，甫營耕桑，有地著之安。

translations.literal: At first we dwelt at Binzhou and had just established farming and sericulture, with the security of settled land.
translations.idiomatic: At first we were stationed at Binzhou and had just begun farming, with the security of settled homes.

sentences.zh: 徙屯涇州，披荊榛，立軍府；

translations.literal: We were moved to encamp at Jingzhou, cleared brambles and thorns, and established the army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: We were moved to Jingzhou, cleared the wilderness, and built our headquarters.

sentences.zh: 坐席未暖，又投之塞外。

translations.literal: Our seats were not yet warm before we were cast out beyond the frontier again.
translations.idiomatic: Our seats were not yet warm before we are cast out beyond the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 吾屬何罪而至此乎！

translations.literal: What crime have we committed to come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: What crime have we committed to deserve this!"

sentences.zh: 」李懷光始為邠寧帥，即誅溫儒雅等，軍令嚴峻。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang when he first became commander of Binning immediately executed Wen Ruya and the others; military law was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang, when he first became commander of Binning, had immediately executed Wen Ruya and the others. His military discipline was severe.

sentences.zh: 及兼涇原，諸將皆懼，曰：「彼五將何罪而為戮？

translations.literal: When he additionally took Jingyuan, the generals were all afraid and said: "What crime did those five generals commit to be slaughtered?
translations.idiomatic: When he additionally took command of Jingyuan, the generals were all afraid. They said, "What crime did those five generals commit to be slaughtered?

sentences.zh: 今又來此，吾屬能無憂乎！

translations.literal: Now he comes here again—can we be without worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Now he comes here again—how can we not worry!"

sentences.zh: 」劉文喜因眾心不安，據涇州，不受詔，上疏復求段秀實為帥，不則朱泚。

translations.literal: Liu Wenxi, taking advantage of the troops' unease, held Jingzhou and did not accept the edict; he memorialized again asking for Duan Xiushi as commander, or else Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxi, taking advantage of the troops' unrest, seized Jingzhou and refused to accept the edict. He memorialized asking for Duan Xiushi as commander, or else Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以朱泚兼四鎮、北庭行軍、涇原節度使，代懷光。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Zhu Ci was additionally made military governor of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court expedition and of Jingyuan, replacing Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, Zhu Ci was appointed military governor of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court expedition and of Jingyuan, replacing Huai'guang.

sentences.zh: 三月，翰林學士、左散騎常侍張涉受前湖南觀察使辛京杲金，事覺；

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhang She, Hanlin academician and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, received gold from Xin Jinggao, former observation commissioner of Hunan; the matter was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang She, Hanlin academician and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was found to have accepted gold from Xin Jinggao, former observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 上怒，欲置於法。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to punish him by law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and wished to punish him by law.

sentences.zh: 時李忠臣以檢校司空、同平章事、奉朝請，言於上曰：「陛下貴為天子，而先生以乏財犯法，以臣愚觀之，非先生之過也。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zhongchen, as acting Minister of Works, Junior Chancellor of equal rank, and court attendant, said to the emperor: "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven, yet the gentleman violated the law from lack of funds—in this servant's foolish view, it is not the gentleman's fault."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Zhongchen, acting Minister of Works and Junior Chancellor, said to the emperor, "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven, yet the gentleman broke the law from poverty. In my foolish view, it is not his fault."

sentences.zh: 」上意解，辛未，放涉歸田裡。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was eased; on the day xinwei, She was released to return to his fields and village.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased. On the day xinwei, She was released to return home.

sentences.zh: 辛京杲以私忿杖殺部曲，有司奏京杲罪當死，上將從之。

translations.literal: Xin Jinggao, from private resentment, beat and killed a subordinate officer; the responsible offices memorialized that Jinggao's crime deserved death, and the emperor was about to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Jinggao had beaten and killed a subordinate officer out of private resentment. The responsible offices memorialized that his crime deserved death, and the emperor was about to agree.

sentences.zh: 李忠臣曰：「京杲當死久矣！

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen said: "Jinggao ought to have died long ago!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen said, "Jinggao ought to have died long ago!"

sentences.zh: 」上問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 忠臣曰：「京杲諸父兄弟皆戰死，獨京杲至今尚存，臣故以為當死久矣。

translations.literal: Zhongchen said: "Jinggao's uncles and brothers all died in battle; only Jinggao survives to this day—your servant therefore holds that he ought to have died long ago."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen said, "Jinggao's uncles and brothers all died in battle. Only Jinggao survives to this day. I therefore hold that he ought to have died long ago."

sentences.zh: 」上憫然，左遷京杲諸王傅。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to pity and demoted Jinggao to tutor of the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to pity and demoted Jinggao to tutor of the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 忠臣乘機救人，多此類。

translations.literal: Zhongchen seized opportunities to save people—many were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen often seized such opportunities to save people—many cases were like this.

sentences.zh: 楊炎罷度支、轉運使，命金部、倉部代之。

translations.literal: Yang Yan abolished the commissioners of revenue and transport and ordered the Gold and Granary bureaus to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan abolished the commissioners of revenue and transport and ordered the Gold and Granary bureaus to take their place.

sentences.zh: 既而省職久廢，耳目不相接，莫能振舉，天下錢穀無所總領。

translations.literal: Soon the provincial duties had long been abandoned; eyes and ears did not connect; none could rouse and lift affairs; money and grain throughout the realm had no overall head.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it became clear that these bureaus had long been neglected, their functions disconnected, and unable to manage affairs. Revenues throughout the realm had no central oversight.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，復以諫議大夫韓洄為戶部侍郎、判度支，以金部郎中萬年杜佑權江、淮水陸轉運使，皆如舊制。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Han Hui, Grand Master of Remonstrance, was again made Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of revenue; Du You of Wannian, director of the Gold Bureau, was made acting commissioner of water and land transport on the Yangtze and Huai—all as in the old system.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Han Hui, Grand Master of Remonstrance, was again appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and acting commissioner of revenue; Du You of Wannian, director of the Gold Bureau, was made acting commissioner of Yangtze and Huai water and land transport—all as under the old system.

sentences.zh: 劉文喜又不受詔，欲自邀旌節；

translations.literal: Liu Wenxi again did not accept the edict and wished to obtain the command baton for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenxi again refused to accept the edict and sought to obtain a military commission for himself.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙未朔，據涇州叛，遣其子質於吐蕃以求援。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of the day yiwei, he held Jingzhou in rebellion and sent his son Zhi to Tibet to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of the day yiwei, he rebelled and held Jingzhou, sending his son Zhi to Tibet to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 上命朱泚、李懷光討之，又命神策軍使張巨濟將禁兵二千助之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhu Ci and Li Huai'guang to attack him and also ordered Zhang Juji, commander of the Divine Strategy Army, to lead two thousand palace guards to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhu Ci and Li Huai'guang to attack him and also ordered Zhang Juji, commander of the Divine Strategy Army, to lead two thousand palace guards to assist.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃始聞韋倫歸其俘，不之信，及俘入境，各還部落，稱：「新天子出宮人，放禽獸，英威聖德，洽於中國。

translations.literal: Tibet at first heard that Wei Lun was returning their captives and did not believe it; when the captives entered the border and each returned to his tribe, they declared: "The new Son of Heaven releases palace women, frees birds and beasts—heroic majesty and sagely virtue pervade China."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet at first did not believe that Wei Lun was returning their captives. When the captives crossed the border and each returned to his tribe, they reported, "The new Son of Heaven has released palace women and freed captive birds and beasts. His heroic majesty and sagely virtue pervade China."

sentences.zh: 」吐蕃大悅，除道迎倫。

translations.literal: Tibet was greatly pleased and cleared the road to welcome Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was greatly pleased and cleared the road to welcome Lun.

sentences.zh: 贊普即發使隨倫入貢，且致賻贈。

translations.literal: The tsanpo immediately sent envoys to follow Lun in presenting tribute and also sent funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan ruler immediately sent envoys to accompany Lun in presenting tribute and also sent funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，至京師，上禮接之。

translations.literal: On guimao, he arrived at the capital; the emperor received him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, he reached the capital, and the emperor welcomed him with full ceremonial courtesy.

sentences.zh: 既而蜀將上言：「吐蕃豺狼，所獲俘不可歸。

translations.literal: Soon after, a Shu general submitted a memorial, saying: 'Tibet is wolves and jackals; the captives we have taken must not be returned.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a Shu general memorialized the throne: 'The Tibetans are wolves and jackals—the captives we have taken must not be sent back.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「戎狄犯塞則擊之，服則歸之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'When the Rong and Di violate the frontier, strike them; when they submit, return them.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'When the barbarians raid the border, we strike them; when they submit, we restore their people.'

sentences.zh: 擊以示威，歸以示信。

translations.literal: Striking shows majesty; returning shows good faith.
translations.idiomatic: To strike is to display might; to return captives is to display trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 威信不立，何以懷遠！

translations.literal: If majesty and good faith are not established, how can one win over those afar!
translations.idiomatic: Without majesty and good faith, how can we bring distant peoples to the throne?

sentences.zh: 」悉命歸之。

translations.literal: He ordered all of them returned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every captive returned.

sentences.zh: 代宗之世，每元日、冬至、端午、生日，州府於常賦之外競為貢獻，貢獻多者則悅之。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Daizong, on each New Year's Day, winter solstice, Dragon Boat Festival, and the emperor's birthday, prefectures and circuits beyond the regular levies competed in presenting tribute; whoever offered more was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Daizong's reign, on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, the Dragon Boat Festival, and the emperor's birthday, prefectures and circuits vied to send tribute beyond the regular levies—and the throne favored those who gave the most.

sentences.zh: 武將、奸吏，緣此侵漁下民。

translations.literal: Military officers and corrupt officials used this as a pretext to plunder the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Military men and corrupt officials used the practice as cover to extort the common people.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，上生日，四方貢獻皆不受。

translations.literal: On guichou, the emperor's birthday, tribute offerings from all quarters were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the emperor's birthday, he refused every tribute gift sent from the four directions.

sentences.zh: 李正己、田悅各獻縑三萬匹，上悉歸之度支以代租賦。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji and Tian Yue each presented thirty thousand bolts of silk; the emperor returned all of it to the Finance Commission in lieu of rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji and Tian Yue each sent thirty thousand bolts of silk; the emperor turned all of it over to the Finance Commission to offset rent and tax obligations.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊辰，以韋倫為太常卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuchen, Wei Lun was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuchen, Wei Lun was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，復遣倫使吐蕃。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Lun was again dispatched as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Lun was again sent as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 倫請上自為載書，與吐蕃盟。

translations.literal: Lun requested that the emperor personally draw up the covenant text to alliance with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Lun asked the emperor to write the alliance covenant himself for a treaty with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 楊炎以為非敵，請與郭子儀輩為載書以聞，令上畫可而已，從之。

translations.literal: Yang Yan considered that improper, and requested that he with Guo Ziyi and the others draw up the covenant text and report it, with the emperor merely marking approval; this was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan judged that inappropriate and asked that he, Guo Ziyi, and others draft the covenant text for the emperor's review, with the emperor need only mark his approval—which the throne accepted.

sentences.zh: 朱泚等圍劉文喜於涇州，杜其出入，而閉壁不與戰，久之不拔。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci and others besieged Liu Wenxi at Jing Prefecture, cut off his coming and going, and shut the walls without joining battle; after a long time they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci and others besieged Liu Wenxi at Jing Prefecture, blockading all entry and exit while holding the walls and refusing battle; months passed without success.

sentences.zh: 天方旱，征發饋運，內外騷然，朝臣上書請赦文喜以蘇疲人者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Heaven was then in drought; levies and transport supply caused turmoil within and without; court officials who submitted memorials asking to pardon Wenxi to relieve the weary people were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: A drought gripped the land; conscription and supply transport threw court and countryside into turmoil, and memorials asking the emperor to pardon Wenxi and spare the exhausted populace became too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 上皆不聽，曰：「微孽不除，何以令天下！

translations.literal: The emperor would not heed any of them, saying: 'If this petty rebel is not removed, how can one command the realm!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused them all, saying, 'If this petty rebel is not eliminated, how can I command the realm!'

sentences.zh: 」文喜使其將劉海賓入奏，海賓言於上曰：「臣乃陛下籓邸部曲，豈肯附叛人，必為陛下梟其首以獻。

translations.literal: Wenxi sent his general Liu Haibin to report to court; Haibin said to the emperor: 'Your servant was a man of Your Majesty's princely household troops—how could I attach myself to a rebel? I will surely take his head for Your Majesty's sake and present it.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenxi sent his general Liu Haibin to report to court. Haibin told the emperor, 'I was one of Your Majesty's household troops when you were still in your princely residence—I would never side with a rebel. I will surely cut off his head and bring it to you.'

sentences.zh: 但文喜今所求者節而已，願陛下姑與之，文喜必怠，則臣計得施矣。

translations.literal: But what Wenxi now seeks is only a commission; I wish Your Majesty would for the moment grant it to him—Wenxi will surely grow slack, and then your servant's plan can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But all Wenxi wants now is a military commission. If Your Majesty would temporarily grant it, he will surely grow careless—and then my plan can succeed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「名器不可假人，爾能立效固善，我節不可得也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Titles and insignia must not be lent to others; if you can achieve results, that is well—but my commission you cannot have.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Rank and insignia are not to be lent out. If you can deliver results, so much the better—but my commission is not for the taking.'

sentences.zh: 」使海賓歸以告文喜，而攻之如初。

translations.literal: He sent Haibin back to tell Wenxi, and pressed the attack as before.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Haibin back to inform Wenxi, and the siege continued as vigorously as before.

sentences.zh: 減御膳以給軍士，城中將士當受春服者，賜予如故。
