translations.literal: He reduced the imperial table to supply the troops; soldiers and officers in the city due to receive spring clothing were granted it as before.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the imperial table to feed the soldiers, and spring clothing due to troops in the besieged city was issued as usual.

sentences.zh: 於是眾知上意不可移。

translations.literal: Thereupon all knew the emperor's resolve could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: From this everyone understood that the emperor's resolve would not budge.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃方睦於唐，不為發兵，城中勢窮。

translations.literal: At that time Tibet was on friendly terms with Tang and did not send troops; within the city their strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was then on good terms with Tang and sent no troops; inside the city, Wenxi's forces were at the end of their rope.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，海賓與諸將共殺文喜，傳首，而原州竟不果城。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Haibin with the other generals jointly killed Wenxi and sent his head; yet the fortification of Yuan Prefecture ultimately was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Haibin and the other generals killed Wenxi and sent his head—but the planned fortification of Yuan Prefecture was never completed after all.

sentences.zh: 自上即位，李正己內不自安，遣參佐入奏事；

translations.literal: From the time the emperor ascended the throne, Li Zhengji was inwardly ill at ease and sent staff members to report on affairs;
translations.idiomatic: From the emperor's accession, Li Zhengji had been inwardly anxious and sent aides to report at court;

sentences.zh: 會涇州捷奏至，上使觀文喜之首而歸。

translations.literal: It happened that the victorious report from Jing Prefecture arrived; the emperor had him view Wenxi's head and then return.
translations.idiomatic: When news of victory at Jing Prefecture arrived, the emperor had the envoy view Wenxi's severed head before sending him home.

sentences.zh: 正己益懼。

translations.literal: Zhengji grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲午朔，門下侍郎、同平章事崔祐甫薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the jiawu new moon, Cui Youfu, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Junior Chancellor of equal rank, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jiawu new moon, Cui Youfu, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Junior Chancellor, died.

sentences.zh: 術士桑道茂上言：「陛下不出數年，暫有離宮之厄。

translations.literal: The adept Sang Daomao submitted a memorial, saying: 'Within a few years Your Majesty will temporarily suffer misfortune at a detached palace.'
translations.idiomatic: The adept Sang Daomao memorialized the throne: 'Within a few years Your Majesty will briefly face calamity at a detached palace.'

sentences.zh: 臣望奉天有天子氣，宜高大其城以備非常。

translations.literal: I observe that Fengtian has the aura of the Son of Heaven; its walls should be raised high to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: I observe an imperial aura over Fengtian; its walls should be raised high against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 」辛丑，命京兆發丁夫數千，雜六軍之士，築奉天城。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the capital prefectural office was ordered to mobilize several thousand corvee laborers, mixed with troops of the Six Armies, to build the walls of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, several thousand corvee laborers from the capital region were mobilized, along with troops of the Six Armies, to build the walls of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 初，回紇風俗樸厚，君臣之等不甚異，故眾志專一，勁健無敵。

translations.literal: At first the Uyghur customs were plain and substantial; ruler and subject were not greatly different in rank, so the common will was unified and their vigor unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Uyghurs lived by plain, sturdy customs; the gap between ruler and subject was not great, so their will was united and their fighters unmatched.

sentences.zh: 及有功於唐，唐賜遺甚厚，登裡可汗始自尊大，築宮殿以居，婦人有粉黛文繡之飾。

translations.literal: After they had merit toward Tang, Tang's gifts were very generous; the Khan Dengli began to esteem himself highly, built palaces to dwell in, and women had powder, rouge, embroidery, and brocade adornments.
translations.idiomatic: After they rendered service to Tang, the court's gifts grew lavish. Khan Dengli began to hold himself above others, built palaces to live in, and his women took up powder, rouge, embroidery, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 中國為之虛耗，而虜俗亦壞。

translations.literal: China was thereby drained, and the barbarian customs also were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: China was drained in the process, and Uyghur ways were corrupted as well.

sentences.zh: 及代宗崩，上遣中使梁文秀往告哀，登裡驕不為禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong died, the emperor sent palace envoy Liang Wenxiu to announce mourning; Dengli was arrogant and showed no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong died, the emperor sent the palace envoy Liang Wenxiu to announce the mourning. Dengli received him arrogantly and without proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 九姓胡附回紇者，說登裡以中國富饒，今乘喪伐之，可有大利。

translations.literal: Nine-Name Sogdians attached to the Uyghurs persuaded Dengli that China was rich and abundant, and that invading now while China was in mourning could bring great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Sogdians of the Nine Surnames attached to the Uyghurs urged Dengli that China was rich and that an invasion during its mourning period could yield great profit.

sentences.zh: 登裡從之，欲舉國入寇。

translations.literal: Dengli followed this advice and wished to mobilize the whole nation in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Dengli took their advice and planned to lead the entire nation in an invasion.

sentences.zh: 其相頓莫賀達干，登裡之從父兄也，諫曰：「唐，大國也，無負於我，吾前年侵太原，獲羊馬數萬，可謂大捷，而道遠糧乏，比歸，士卒多徒行者。

translations.literal: His chancellor Dunmohe Daghan, Dengli's paternal cousin, remonstrated, saying: 'Tang is a great state and has not wronged us. Two years ago we invaded Taiyuan and took tens of thousands of sheep and horses—a great victory, to be sure—but the road was long and provisions scarce; by the time we returned, many soldiers were on foot.'
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor Dunmohe Daghan, Dengli's paternal cousin, remonstrated: 'Tang is a great power that has done us no wrong. Two years ago we raided Taiyuan and seized tens of thousands of sheep and horses—a splendid victory—but the roads were long and supplies short; on the march home many soldiers were afoot.'

sentences.zh: 今舉國深入，萬一不捷，將安歸乎！

translations.literal: Now to lead the whole nation deep into their territory—if by any chance we do not prevail, where shall we return!
translations.idiomatic: If we now plunge the whole nation deep into their country and fortune turns against us, where will we go home to?

sentences.zh: 」登裡不聽。

translations.literal: Dengli would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Dengli would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 頓莫賀乘人心之不欲南寇也，舉兵擊殺之，並九姓胡二千人，自立為合骨咄祿毘伽可汗，遣其臣聿達干與梁文秀俱入見，願為籓臣，垂發不翦，以待冊命。

translations.literal: Dunmohe, taking advantage of the people's unwillingness to raid south, raised troops and killed him, along with two thousand Nine-Name Sogdians; he installed himself as Qaghan Qutluq Bilge, sent his minister Yudagan with Liang Wenxiu together to audience, wished to become a tributary subject, kept his hair uncut, and awaited investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Dunmohe, seizing on widespread reluctance to raid south, raised troops and killed him along with two thousand Sogdians of the Nine Surnames. He proclaimed himself Qaghan Qutluq Bilge, sent his minister Yudagan to audience together with Liang Wenxiu, declared himself willing to become a tributary subject, left his hair uncut in submission, and awaited formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，命京兆少尹臨漳源休冊頓莫賀為武義成功可汗。

translations.literal: On yimao, Yuan Xiu of Linzhang, Vice Prefect of the Capital, was ordered to invest Dunmohe as Wuyi Chenggong Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Yuan Xiu of Linzhang, Vice Prefect of the Capital, was ordered to invest Dunmohe as Qaghan Wuyi Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅，邵州賊帥王國良降。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the bandit chief Wang Guoliang of Shao Prefecture surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, Wang Guoliang, bandit leader in Shao Prefecture, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 國良本湖南牙將，觀察使辛京杲使戍武岡，以扞西原蠻。

translations.literal: Guoliang had originally been a guard officer of Hunan; the surveillance commissioner Xin Jinggao had stationed him at Wugang to repel the Xiyuan Man.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang had been a guard officer in Hunan; surveillance commissioner Xin Jinggao posted him at Wugang to hold back the Xiyuan tribes.

sentences.zh: 京杲貪暴，國良家富，京杲以死罪加之。

translations.literal: Jinggao was greedy and cruel; Guoliang's family was wealthy, and Jinggao charged him with a capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: Jinggao was greedy and brutal. Guoliang's family was wealthy, and Jinggao charged him with a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 國良懼，據縣叛，與西原蠻合，聚眾千人，侵掠州縣，瀕湖千里，咸被其害。

translations.literal: Guoliang was afraid, seized the county and rebelled, joined with the Xiyuan Man, gathered a thousand men, and raided prefectures and counties; for a thousand li along the lakeshore all suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Guoliang seized the county and rebelled, joined the Xiyuan tribes, gathered a thousand followers, and raided prefectures and counties—a thousand li of lakeshore suffered their depredations.

sentences.zh: 詔荊、黔、洪、桂諸道合兵討之，連年不能克。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuits of Jing, Qian, Hong, and Gui to combine forces to attack him; for years they could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Jing, Qian, Hong, and Gui circuits to combine forces against him; year after year they failed to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 及曹王皋為湖南觀察使，曰：「驅疲□，誅反仄，非策之得者也。

translations.literal: When Prince of Cao Gao became Hunan surveillance commissioner, he said: 'Driving the weary people, punishing rebels—this is not a winning strategy.'
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Cao Gao became Hunan surveillance commissioner, he said, 'Driving exhausted troops to crush rebels is not a winning strategy.'

sentences.zh: 」乃遺國良書，言：「將軍非敢為逆，欲救死耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Guoliang a letter, saying: 'General, you did not dare rebellion—you sought only to save your life.'
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guoliang a letter: 'General, you did not set out to rebel—you only wanted to save your life.'

sentences.zh: 我與將軍俱為辛京杲所構，我已蒙聖朝湔洗，何心復加兵刃於將軍乎！

translations.literal: The general and I were both framed by Xin Jinggao; I have already been cleansed by the holy court—what heart would I have to again set arms against the general!
translations.idiomatic: Both of us were framed by Xin Jinggao. The court has already cleared my name—why would I turn weapons on you again!

sentences.zh: 將軍遇我，不速降，後悔無及！

translations.literal: If the general meets me and does not swiftly surrender, there will be no time for regret!
translations.idiomatic: If you meet me and do not surrender at once, you will regret it too late!

sentences.zh: 」國良且喜且懼，遣使乞降，猶疑未決。

translations.literal: Guoliang was both pleased and afraid; he sent envoys to beg surrender but still hesitated without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang was both heartened and afraid; he sent envoys to offer surrender but still could not bring himself to decide.

sentences.zh: 皋乃假為使者，從一騎，越五百里，抵國良壁，鞭其門，大呼曰：「我曹王也，來受降！

translations.literal: Gao then disguised himself as an envoy, with a single horseman, crossed five hundred li, reached Guoliang's fortress, whipped at the gate, and shouted: 'I am Prince of Cao—come to accept your surrender!'
translations.idiomatic: Gao then posed as an envoy, rode with a single companion five hundred li to Guoliang's camp, whipped the gate, and shouted, 'I am Prince of Cao—I have come to accept your surrender!'

sentences.zh: 」舉軍大驚。

translations.literal: The whole army was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The entire force was stunned.

sentences.zh: 國良趨出，迎拜請罪。

translations.literal: Guoliang hurried out, welcomed him with bows, and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang rushed out, bowed in welcome, and pleaded for pardon.

sentences.zh: 皋執其手，約為兄弟，盡焚攻守之具，散其眾，使還農。

translations.literal: Gao took his hand, pledged brotherhood, burned all siege and defense equipment, dispersed his followers, and sent them back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Gao took his hand, pledged brotherhood, burned all weapons of siege and defense, dispersed the rebels, and sent them back to the fields.

sentences.zh: 詔赦國良罪，賜名惟新。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Guoliang's crime and bestowed the name Weixin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Guoliang and bestowed the name Weixin.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，遙尊上母沈氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the emperor's mother, Lady Shen, was honored from afar as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the emperor's mother, Lady Shen, was honored at a distance as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使庾准希楊炎指，奏忠州刺史劉晏與朱泚書求營救，辭多怨望，又奏召補州兵，欲拒朝命，炎證成之。

translations.literal: Jingnan military commissioner Yu Zhun, hoping to please Yang Yan, memorialized that Liu Yan, prefect of Zhong Prefecture, had written Zhu Ci seeking rescue, with language full of resentment, and also memorialized that he had summoned and replenished prefectural troops intending to resist court orders; Yan corroborated it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan military commissioner Yu Zhun, seeking to curry favor with Yang Yan, memorialized that Liu Yan, prefect of Zhong Prefecture, had written Zhu Ci begging rescue in resentful terms, and further that Yan had raised local troops to resist imperial orders; Yang Yan backed the accusation.

sentences.zh: 上密遣中使就忠州縊殺之，己丑，乃下詔賜死。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent a palace envoy to Zhong Prefecture to strangle him; on jichou, an edict was then issued granting death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent a palace envoy to Zhong Prefecture to strangle him; on jichou an edict formally ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 天下冤之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The empire regarded it as a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 初，安、史之亂，數年間，天下戶口什亡八九，州縣多為籓鎮所據，貢賦不入，朝廷府庫耗竭，中國多故，戎狄每歲犯邊，所在宿重兵，仰給縣官，所費不貲，皆倚辦於晏。

translations.literal: At first, in the An and Shi rebellion, within several years nine or eight tenths of the realm's registered households perished; many prefectures and counties were seized by military governors, tribute and tax did not enter the court, the imperial treasury was exhausted, China had many troubles, and the Rong and Di each year violated the border; everywhere heavy garrisons were posted, relying on the government for supply—the cost was incalculable—and all depended on Yan to provide it.
translations.idiomatic: In the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellion, within a few years eight or nine households in ten vanished from the registers; prefectures and counties fell to military governors, tribute ceased to reach the court, and the imperial treasury ran dry. China was beset by troubles, and barbarians raided the frontier every year. Heavy garrisons everywhere depended on the state for supplies at ruinous cost—and all of it had to be managed through Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏初為轉運使，獨領陝東諸道，陝西皆度支領之，末年兼領，未幾而罷。

translations.literal: When Yan first served as transport commissioner, he alone oversaw the circuits east of Shan; west of Shan was overseen by the Finance Commission; in his final years he held both, and soon after was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first became transport commissioner, he alone oversaw the circuits east of Shan; the Finance Commission handled the west. In his final years he held both portfolios, but was dismissed not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 晏有精力，多機智，變通有無，曲盡其妙。

translations.literal: Yan had abundant energy and much ingenuity; in adapting presence and absence he exhaustively mastered the subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was tireless and ingenious, adapting supply to demand with masterly finesse.

sentences.zh: 常以厚直募善走者，置遞相望，覘報四方物價，雖遠方，不數日皆達使司，食貨輕重之權，悉制在掌握，國家獲利，而天下無甚貴甚賤之憂。

translations.literal: He constantly recruited swift runners at generous pay, stationed relay posts in sight of one another, and reconnoitered prices of goods in the four directions; even distant places reached the commissioner's office within a few days, and the weight of commodity prices was wholly controlled in his grasp—the state profited, and the realm had no worry of things being extremely dear or extremely cheap.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly hired fast runners at generous wages and set relay posts within sight of one another to report prices across the empire. Even distant markets reached his office within days, and the leverage over commodity prices rested entirely in his hands—the state profited, and the realm was spared wild swings in price.

sentences.zh: 常以為：「辦集眾務，在於得人，故必擇通敏、精悍、廉勤之士而用之；

translations.literal: He constantly held: 'To assemble many tasks lies in obtaining men; therefore one must select men who are penetrating, keen, incorruptible, and diligent and employ them;'
translations.idiomatic: He always maintained that managing many affairs depended on finding the right people, and so he chose men who were sharp, capable, honest, and diligent;

sentences.zh: 至於句檢簿書、出納錢穀，事雖至細，必委之士類；

translations.literal: as for examining ledgers, disbursing and receiving money and grain—even matters extremely minute—he always entrusted them to gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: even the minute work of auditing ledgers and handling cash and grain he entrusted to educated officials;

sentences.zh: 吏惟書符牒，不得輕出一言。

translations.literal: clerks only copied documents and were not permitted lightly to utter a word.
translations.idiomatic: clerks merely copied documents and were not allowed to speak out of turn.

sentences.zh: 」常言：「士陷贓賄，則淪棄於時，名重於利，故士多清修；

translations.literal: He often said: 'When gentlemen fall into bribery, they are cast aside by the age; reputation weighs heavier than profit, so gentlemen mostly keep themselves pure;'
translations.idiomatic: He often said, 'When gentlemen take bribes, they are ruined for life—reputation matters more than profit, so gentlemen tend toward integrity;'

sentences.zh: 吏雖潔廉，終無顯榮，利重於名，故吏多貪污。

translations.literal: though clerks may be clean and incorruptible, in the end they win no conspicuous glory; profit weighs heavier than reputation, so clerks mostly are corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: 'clerks may stay clean, but they win no real glory—profit matters more than reputation, so clerks tend toward corruption.'

sentences.zh: 」然惟晏能行之，它人效者終莫能逮。

translations.literal: Yet only Yan could carry this out; others who imitated him in the end could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yan could make this system work; others who tried to copy him never matched him.

sentences.zh: 其屬官雖居數千里外，奉教令如在目前，起居語言，無敢欺紿。

translations.literal: His subordinate officials, though stationed thousands of li away, received his instructions as if he were before their eyes; in daily conduct and speech none dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates thousands of li away carried out his orders as if he stood before them; in daily conduct and speech none dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 當時權貴，或以親故屬之者，晏亦應之，使俸給多少，遷次緩速，皆如其志，然無得親職事。

translations.literal: Powerful nobles of the time sometimes recommended relatives and friends to him; Yan also accepted them, letting salary and rank, pace of promotion, and timing accord with their wishes—yet they could not hold substantive posts.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful nobles sometimes recommended relatives and friends; Yan accepted them and adjusted salary, rank, and promotion to their wishes—but never gave them substantive responsibility.

sentences.zh: 其場院要劇之官，必盡一時之選。

translations.literal: For important and demanding posts at the transport depots, he always chose the best men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: For the demanding posts at his transport depots he always chose the best men available.

sentences.zh: 故晏沒之後，掌財賦有聲者，多晏之故吏也。

translations.literal: Therefore after Yan died, those who gained renown in managing finances were mostly his former clerks.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's death, most officials who won renown in finance had served under him.

sentences.zh: 晏又以為戶口滋多，則賦稅自廣，故其理財常以養民為先。

translations.literal: Yan also held that when households multiply, tax revenue naturally broadens; therefore in managing finances he always put nourishing the people first.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also held that as households multiplied, tax revenue would naturally expand; in managing finances he always put the welfare of the people first.

sentences.zh: 諸道各置知院官，每旬月，具州縣雨雪豐歉之狀白使司，豐則貴糴，歉則賤糶，或以谷易雜貨供官用，及於豐處賣之。

translations.literal: Each circuit set intake officers; every ten-day period they reported to the commissioner's office the condition of rain, snow, abundance, and shortage in prefectures and counties; in abundance they bought grain dear, in shortage they sold grain cheap, or exchanged grain for miscellaneous goods to supply official needs, and in abundant places sold it.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit appointed intake officers who, every ten days, reported rainfall, snow, harvests, and shortages to his office. In good years he bought grain at fair prices; in bad years he sold it cheaply, exchanged grain for other goods to meet official needs, or sold reserves where harvests were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 知院官始見不稔之端，先申，至某月須如干蠲免，某月須如干救助，及期，晏不俟州縣申請，即奏行之，應民之急，未嘗失時，不待其困弊、流亡、餓殍，然後賑之也。

translations.literal: When intake officers first saw signs of poor harvest, they reported in advance that in such-and-such a month so much remission would be needed and in such-and-such a month so much relief; when the time came, Yan did not wait for prefectures and counties to apply—he memorialized and carried it out, responding to the people's urgency and never missing the season, not waiting until they were exhausted, displaced, or starving before giving relief.
translations.idiomatic: When intake officers first detected poor harvests, they reported in advance how much tax relief would be needed in a given month and how much aid in another. When the time came, Yan did not wait for local applications—he memorialized and acted at once, meeting the people's needs without delay, rather than waiting until they were ruined, displaced, or starving.

sentences.zh: 由是民得安其居業，戶口蕃息。

translations.literal: Thereby the people were able to settle in their occupations, and registered households increased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were able to keep their livelihoods, and registered households grew.

sentences.zh: 晏始為轉運使，時天下見戶不過二百萬，其季年乃三百餘萬；

translations.literal: When Yan first became transport commissioner, registered households under Heaven did not exceed two million; in his final years they reached more than three million;
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first became transport commissioner, registered households nationwide numbered no more than two million; by his final years they exceeded three million;

sentences.zh: 在晏所統則增，非晏所統則不增也。

translations.literal: where Yan oversaw, they increased; where Yan did not oversee, they did not increase.
translations.idiomatic: where he had authority, numbers rose; where he did not, they did not.

sentences.zh: 其初財賦歲入不過四百萬緡，季年乃千餘萬緡。

translations.literal: At first annual revenue from finances did not exceed four million strings of cash; in his final years it reached more than ten million strings.
translations.idiomatic: At first annual fiscal revenue did not exceed four million strings of cash; by his final years it exceeded ten million.

sentences.zh: 晏專用榷鹽法充軍國之用。

translations.literal: Yan relied exclusively on the salt monopoly system to meet military and state needs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan relied chiefly on the salt monopoly to meet military and state needs.

sentences.zh: 時自許、汝、鄭、鄧之西，皆食河東池鹽，度支主之；

translations.literal: At that time from Xu, Ru, Zheng, and Deng westward all ate Hedong pond salt, overseen by the Finance Commission;
translations.idiomatic: At that time from Xu, Ru, Zheng, and Deng westward all consumed Hedong pond salt under the Finance Commission;

sentences.zh: 汴、滑、唐、蔡之東，皆食海鹽，晏主之。

translations.literal: east of Bian, Hua, Tang, and Cai all ate sea salt, overseen by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: east of Bian, Hua, Tang, and Cai all consumed sea salt under Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏以為官多則民擾，故但於出鹽之鄉置鹽官，收鹽戶所煮之鹽轉鬻於商人，任其所之，自餘州縣不復置官。

translations.literal: Yan held that many officials would disturb the people; therefore he only placed salt officials in salt-producing districts, collected the salt boiled by salt households, and resold it to merchants, letting them take it where they would; the remaining prefectures and counties no longer placed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held that too many officials would harass the people; he therefore placed salt officials only in producing districts, bought salt from salt households, and resold it to merchants who could carry it wherever they chose—other prefectures and counties had no salt offices.

sentences.zh: 其江嶺間去鹽鄉遠者，轉官鹽於彼貯之。

translations.literal: In the Jiang and Ling regions far from salt districts, official salt was transported and stored there.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiang and Ling regions far from salt districts, he shipped and stored official salt locally.

sentences.zh: 或商絕鹽貴，則減價鬻之，謂之常平鹽，官獲其利而民不乏鹽。

translations.literal: If merchants cut off supply and salt grew dear, the price was reduced and sold—called Ever-Normal salt; the state gained profit and the people lacked no salt.
translations.idiomatic: When merchants withheld supply and salt grew dear, he cut prices and sold reserves—the so-called Ever-Normal salt—so the state profited and the people were not left without salt.

sentences.zh: 其始江、淮鹽利不過四十萬緡，季年乃六百餘萬緡，由是國用充足而民不困弊。

translations.literal: At first profit from Jiang and Huai salt did not exceed four hundred thousand strings; in his final years it reached more than six million strings; thereby state use was sufficient and the people were not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: At first profit from Jiang and Huai salt did not exceed four hundred thousand strings; by his final years it exceeded six million—enough to meet state needs without burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 其河東鹽利，不過八十萬緡，而價復貴於海鹽。

translations.literal: Profit from Hedong salt did not exceed eight hundred thousand strings, yet its price was again dearer than sea salt.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong salt yielded no more than eight hundred thousand strings, yet its price remained higher than sea salt.

sentences.zh: 先是，運關東谷入長安者，以河流湍悍，率一斛得八斗至者，則為成勞，受優賞。

translations.literal: Previously, in transporting Guandong grain into Chang'an, because the river current was swift and fierce, generally if eight dou in ten of a hu arrived it counted as full labor and received preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, grain shipped from Guandong to Chang'an faced fierce river currents; if eight tenths of a load arrived intact, the haul counted as full service and earned premium pay.

sentences.zh: 晏以為江、汴、河、渭，水力不同，各隨便宜，造運船，教漕卒，江船達揚州，汴船達河陰，河船達渭口，渭船達太倉，其間緣水置倉，轉相受給。

translations.literal: Yan held that the Jiang, Bian, Yellow, and Wei rivers differed in water power; each followed convenience, built transport ships, and trained transport soldiers—Jiang ships reached Yangzhou, Bian ships reached Heyin, river ships reached the Wei mouth, Wei ships reached the Great Granary; between them warehouses were placed along the water to receive and supply in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yan recognized that the Yangzi, Bian Canal, Yellow, and Wei rivers differed in force; he built ships suited to each, trained transport crews, and linked the routes—Yangzi ships to Yangzhou, Bian ships to Heyin, Yellow River ships to the Wei mouth, Wei ships to the Great Granary—with granaries along the waterways to transfer cargo in stages.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲運谷或至百餘萬斛，無斗升沉覆者。

translations.literal: From this each year grain transported sometimes reached more than a million hu, with not a dou or sheng lost or capsized.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter annual grain shipments sometimes exceeded a million hu without losing a single measure to spill or capsizing.

sentences.zh: 船十艘為一綱，使軍將領之，十運無失，授優勞，官其人。

translations.literal: Ten ships formed one convoy, led by a military commander; if ten transport runs passed without loss, superior reward was granted and the man was given an official post.
translations.idiomatic: Ten ships formed one convoy under a military commander; after ten successful runs without loss, he received special reward and an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 數運之後，無不斑白者。

translations.literal: After several runs, none were not streaked with gray.
translations.idiomatic: After several runs, none of the transport workers were without gray in their hair.

sentences.zh: 晏於揚子置十場造船，每艘給錢千緡。

translations.literal: Yan set up ten shipyards at Yangzi and gave a thousand strings of cash for each vessel built.
translations.idiomatic: Yan established ten shipyards on the Yangzi and paid a thousand strings of cash for each vessel built.

sentences.zh: 或言「所用實不及半，虛費太多。

translations.literal: Some said, 'What was actually used did not reach half—empty waste was too great.'
translations.idiomatic: Some complained, 'The actual cost was less than half that—far too much was wasted.'

sentences.zh: 」晏曰：「不然，論大計者固不可惜小費，凡事必為永久之慮。

translations.literal: Yan said: 'It is not so. Those who reckon the grand plan must not begrudge small expense; in all things one must plan for permanence.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, 'Not so. Those who think in grand terms must not stint on small costs; every undertaking must be built to last.

sentences.zh: 今始置船場，執事者至多，當先使之私用無窘，則官物堅牢矣。

translations.literal: Now that shipyards are first being established, those in charge are very numerous; they should first be allowed private use without hardship—then official goods will be solid and durable.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that shipyards are being set up, there are many overseers; if they are first allowed enough for their private needs, the state's vessels will be solid and durable.'

sentences.zh: 若遽與之屑屑校計錙銖，安能久行乎！

translations.literal: If one hastily with them minutely reconciles every ounce and grain, how can it long be carried out!
translations.idiomatic: If we start haggling over every penny with them from the outset, how can the system endure?

sentences.zh: 異日必有患吾所給多而減之者；

translations.literal: Someday there will surely be those who worry that what we give is too much and reduce it;
translations.idiomatic: Sooner or later someone will complain that we give too much and cut the allowance;

sentences.zh: 減半以下猶可也，過此則不能運矣。

translations.literal: Reducing by half or less would still be tolerable; beyond that it could not operate.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting it by half or less might still work; beyond that, transport would collapse.

sentences.zh: 」其後五十年，有司果減其半。

translations.literal: '" Fifty years later, the officials indeed reduced it by half.
translations.idiomatic: '" Fifty years later, the officials did in fact cut the payment in half.

sentences.zh: 及咸通中，有司計費而給之，無復羨餘，船益脆薄易壞，漕運遂廢矣。

translations.literal: By the Xiantong era, officials calculated costs and disbursed accordingly, with no surplus remaining; ships grew ever flimsier and easier to break, and grain transport was eventually abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xiantong period, officials paid only calculated costs with no surplus; ships grew ever thinner and more fragile, and the canal transport system was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 晏為人勤力，事無閒劇，必於一日中決之，不使留宿，後來言財利者皆莫能及之。

translations.literal: Yan as a man was diligent; affairs whether minor or major he necessarily decided within a single day and did not let them remain overnight; later men who spoke of finances and profit were none able to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was tireless: whether a matter was trivial or urgent, he settled it within the day and never let business overnight. Later experts in finance could not match him.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲午，振武留後張光晟殺回紇使者突董等九百餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jiawu, Zhang Guangsheng, acting prefect of Zhenwu, killed the Uyghur envoy Tu Chong and more than nine hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu, Zhang Guangsheng, acting prefect of Zhenwu, slaughtered the Uyghur envoy Tu Chong and more than nine hundred of his party.

sentences.zh: 突董者，武義可汗之叔父也。

translations.literal: Tu Chong was the paternal uncle of the Martial Righteousness Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Chong was the uncle of the Martial Righteousness Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 代宗之世，九姓胡常冒回紇之名，雜居京師，殖貨縱暴，與回紇共為公私之患。

translations.literal: In Emperor Daizong's reign, Nine-Name Sogdians often usurped the Uyghur name, mingled in the capital, amassed goods and indulged in violence, and together with the Uyghurs became a public and private affliction.
translations.idiomatic: During Daizong's reign, Sogdians of the Nine Surnames often passed themselves off as Uyghurs, lived in the capital, amassed wealth, and committed violence. Together with the Uyghurs they were a plague on public and private life alike.

sentences.zh: 上即位，命突董盡帥其徒歸國，輜重甚盛。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he ordered Tu Chong to lead all his followers home; their baggage train was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor acceded, he ordered Tu Chong to lead all his followers home. Their train of baggage was immense.

sentences.zh: 至振武，留數月，厚求資給，日食肉千斤，他物稱是，縱樵牧者暴踐果稼，振武人苦之。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhenwu, they stayed several months, demanding generous supplies; each day they consumed a thousand jin of meat, and other goods in proportion; they allowed woodcutters and herders to trample fruit and grain wantonly; the people of Zhenwu suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenwu they lingered for months, demanding lavish provisions--a thousand jin of meat daily, with other supplies to match--and let woodcutters and herders ravage orchards and crops. The people of Zhenwu were driven to misery.

sentences.zh: 光晟欲殺回紇，取其輜重，而畏其眾強，未敢發。

translations.literal: Guangsheng wished to kill the Uyghurs and seize their baggage train, but feared their numbers and strength and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsheng wanted to kill the Uyghurs and seize their baggage, but feared their numbers and held back.

sentences.zh: 九姓胡聞其種族為新可汗所誅，多道亡，突董防之甚急。

translations.literal: The Nine-Name Sogdians, hearing that their clansmen had been executed by the new qaghan, many fled by the roads; Tu Chong guarded against them very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the new qaghan had executed many of their kin, the Nine-Name Sogdians fled in numbers; Tu Chong guarded them closely.

sentences.zh: 九姓胡不得亡，又不敢歸，乃密獻策於光晟，請殺回紇。

translations.literal: The Nine-Name Sogdians, unable to flee yet not daring to return, secretly offered Guangsheng a plan, asking to kill the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped--unable to flee yet afraid to return--the Nine-Name Sogdians secretly urged Guangsheng to slaughter the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 光晟喜其黨類自離，許之。

translations.literal: Guangsheng was pleased that their faction split of itself and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsheng was pleased to see their faction split from within and agreed.

sentences.zh: 上以陝州之辱，心恨回紇。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of the humiliation at Shaanzhou, bore hatred for the Uyghurs in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still resented the Uyghurs for the humiliation at Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 光晟知上旨，乃奏稱：「回紇本種非多，所輔以強者，群胡耳。

translations.literal: Guangsheng, knowing the emperor's intent, memorialized, saying: 'The Uyghur stock itself is not numerous; what makes them strong is the mass of Sogdian tribes alone.'
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor's mind, Guangsheng memorialized: 'The Uyghurs themselves are not numerous; their strength comes only from the surrounding Sogdian tribes.'

sentences.zh: 今聞其自相魚肉，頓莫賀新立，移地健有孽子，及國相、梅金錄各擁兵數千人相攻，國未定。

translations.literal: Now I hear they devour one another; Tun Mohe has newly been installed; Yidijian has a bastard son; and the chief minister Mei Jinlu each holds several thousand troops and attacks the other--the state is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: I hear they are now tearing one another apart: Tun Mohe has just ascended; Yidijian has a bastard son; and Chief Minister Mei Jinlu each leads thousands of troops against the others--the realm is still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 彼無財則不能使其眾，陛下不乘此際除之，乃歸其人，與之財，正所謂借寇兵繼盜糧者也。

translations.literal: Without wealth they cannot command their masses; if Your Majesty does not seize this moment to eliminate them, but returns their men and gives them wealth, that is precisely what is called lending arms to the enemy and supplying grain to robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Without money they cannot control their followers. If Your Majesty does not destroy them now but sends their men home with funds, you will be arming bandits and feeding thieves--as the proverb says.

sentences.zh: 請殺之。

translations.literal: I request that they be killed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be killed.

sentences.zh: 」三奏，上不許。

translations.literal: '" He memorialized three times; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: '" Three times he memorialized; three times the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 光晟乃使副將過其館門，故不為禮；

translations.literal: Guangsheng then had a deputy general pass their lodge gate and deliberately show no courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: Guangsheng then sent a deputy past their lodge and deliberately omitted the proper courtesy;

sentences.zh: 突董怒，執而鞭之數十。

translations.literal: Tu Chong was angry, seized him, and flogged him several dozen times.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Chong flew into a rage, seized the man, and flogged him dozens of times.

sentences.zh: 光晟勒兵掩擊，並群胡盡殺之，聚為京觀。

translations.literal: Guangsheng marshaled troops for a surprise attack, killed all the Sogdian tribes together, and piled them into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsheng launched a surprise attack, slaughtered the Uyghurs and all the allied Sogdians, and piled the corpses into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 獨留二胡，使歸國為證，曰：「回紇鞭辱大將，且謀襲據振武，故先事誅之。

translations.literal: He alone kept two Sogdians, sent them home as witnesses, saying: 'The Uyghurs flogged and humiliated a general and plotted to seize Zhenwu; therefore I executed them first.'
translations.idiomatic: He spared two Sogdians to bear witness home, saying: 'The Uyghurs flogged and humiliated my deputy and plotted to seize Zhenwu, so I acted first.'

sentences.zh: 」上征光晟為右金吾將軍，遣中使王嘉祥征致信幣。

translations.literal: '" The emperor summoned Guangsheng as General of the Right Golden Guard and sent the palace envoy Wang Jiaxiang to convey letters and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor summoned Guangsheng to serve as General of the Right Golden Guard and sent the palace envoy Wang Jiaxiang with letters and gifts.

sentences.zh: 回紇請得專殺者以復仇，上為之貶光晟為睦王傅以慰其意。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs requested the right to execute the killer for revenge; the emperor for their sake demoted Guangsheng to Tutor of the Prince of Mu to assuage them.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs demanded the right to execute the killer in revenge; to appease them the emperor demoted Guangsheng to Tutor of the Prince of Mu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，加盧龍、隴右、涇原節度使朱泚兼中書令，盧龍、隴右節度如故。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, Zhu Ci, military governor of Lulong, Longyou, and Jingyuan, was additionally made Grand Counselor; his governorships of Lulong and Longyou remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Zhu Ci, military governor of Lulong, Longyou, and Jingyuan, was also made Grand Counselor; he retained his Lulong and Longyou commands.

sentences.zh: 以舒王謨為四鎮、北庭行軍、涇原節度大使，以涇州牙前兵馬使河中姚令言為留後。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu, Mo, was made Grand Commissioner of the Four Garrisons, Beiting Field Army, and Jingyuan Circuit; Yao Lingyan of Hezhong, chief of the Jingzhou advanced troops, was made acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu, Mo, was appointed Grand Commissioner for the Four Garrisons, Beiting Field Army, and Jingyuan Circuit; Yao Lingyan of Hezhong, chief of the Jingzhou advanced troops, was made acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 謨，邈之子也，早孤，上子之。

translations.literal: Mo was the son of Yao; orphaned early, the emperor treated him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was Yao's son; orphaned young, the emperor had raised him as his own.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔贈太后父、祖、兄、弟官，及自餘宗族男女拜官封邑者告第告身，凡百二十有七通；

translations.literal: On the day guichou, an edict conferred posthumous offices on the Empress Dowager's father, grandfather, brothers, and younger brothers, and certificates of residence and appointment for all other clansmen and clanswomen granted office and fiefs--one hundred twenty-seven in all;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, an edict posthumously ennobled the Empress Dowager's father, grandfather, brothers, and kin, and issued one hundred twenty-seven certificates of residence and appointment for other relatives ennobled or granted fiefs;

sentences.zh: 中使以馬負而賜之。

translations.literal: Palace envoys carried them on horses and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys delivered them by horseback.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬午，將作奏宣政殿廊壞，十月魁岡，未可修。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day renwu, the Directorate of Works reported that the corridor of the Xuanzheng Hall was damaged; in the tenth month the Kui Ridge would be ascendant--it was not yet suitable to repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renwu, the Directorate of Works reported that the Xuanzheng Hall corridor had collapsed; with the Kui Ridge ascendant in the tenth month, repairs were inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「但不妨公害人，則吉矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'So long as it does not harm people or obstruct public business, that is auspicious enough.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'So long as it does not harm people or obstruct public business, that is auspicious enough.'

sentences.zh: 安問時日！

translations.literal: Why ask about the calendar day!
translations.idiomatic: Why quibble over the calendar!

sentences.zh: 」即命修之。

translations.literal: '" He immediately ordered repairs.
translations.idiomatic: '" He ordered repairs at once.

sentences.zh: 大歷以前，賦斂出納俸給皆無法，長吏得專之；

translations.literal: Before the Dali era, taxation, disbursement, receipt, and salary payment all had no fixed law; chief officials could dispose of them at will;
translations.idiomatic: Before Dali, taxation, collection, and salary payment followed no fixed rules; local chiefs did as they pleased;

sentences.zh: 重以元、王秉政，貨賂公行，天下不按贓吏者殆二十年。

translations.literal: Compounded by Yuan and Wang holding power, bribes ran openly; throughout the realm corrupt officials were scarcely prosecuted--for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuan and Wang in power, bribery flourished openly, and for nearly twenty years corrupt officials across the empire went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 惟江西觀察使路嗣恭案虔州刺史源敷翰，流之。

translations.literal: Only Lu Sigong, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, investigated Yuan Fuhan, prefect of Qianzhou, and banished him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lu Sigong, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, investigated Qianzhou Prefect Yuan Fuhan and banished him.

sentences.zh: 上以宣歙觀察使薛邕，文雅舊臣，徵為左丞。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Xue Yong, observation commissioner of Xuan and She, an elegant old minister, summoned him as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xue Yong, observation commissioner of Xuan and She and a cultivated elder statesman, to serve as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 邕去宣州，盜隱官物以巨萬計，殿中侍御史員□發之。

translations.literal: When Yong left Xuanzhou, he had concealed official goods amounting to tens of thousands; Palace Attendant Censor Yuan □ exposed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong left Xuanzhou, he had embezzled official goods worth tens of thousands; Palace Attendant Censor Yuan □ exposed the crime.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，貶連山尉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jihai, he was demoted to captain of Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on jihai, he was demoted to captain of Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 於是州縣始畏朝典，不敢放縱。

translations.literal: Thereupon prefectures and counties first feared court law and did not dare act unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After that, prefectures and counties began to fear the court's authority and dared not abuse their power.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，疏斥宦官，親任朝士，而張涉以儒學入侍，薛邕以文雅登朝，繼以贓敗。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, he kept eunuchs at a distance and personally trusted court scholars; Zhang She entered attendance through Confucian learning, Xue Yong rose through cultured elegance--both were soon ruined by corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign the emperor distanced eunuchs and trusted court scholars; Zhang She rose through Confucian learning and Xue Yong through cultivated elegance--yet both were soon disgraced by corruption.

sentences.zh: 宦官武將得以借口，曰：「南牙文臣贓動至巨萬，而謂我曹濁亂天下，豈非期罔邪！

translations.literal: Eunuchs and military officers gained their excuse, saying: 'Civil officials of the Southern Bureau amass fortunes of tens of thousands, yet say we have befouled the realm--is that not bare deceit!'
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and generals seized their excuse: 'Southern Bureau civilians steal fortunes in the tens of thousands, yet claim we have ruined the realm--is that not a lie!'

sentences.zh: 」於是上心始疑，不知所倚杖矣。

translations.literal: '" Thereupon doubt first arose in the emperor's heart, and he no longer knew whom to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: '" From then on the emperor began to doubt, no longer sure whom he could trust.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人高參請分遣諸沈訪求太后，庚寅，以睦王述為奉迎使，工部尚書喬琳副之，又命諸沈四人為判官，與中使分行諸道求之。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Sheren Gao Can requested dispatching the various Shen clansmen to search for the Empress Dowager; on the day gengyin, the Prince of Mu, Shu, was made welcoming commissioner, with Minister of Works Qiao Lin as deputy; four Shen clansmen were also appointed adjudicators, who with palace envoys traveled the circuits separately to seek her.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Can, a drafting officer, proposed sending members of the Shen clan to search for the Empress Dowager. On gengyin the Prince of Mu, Shu, was named welcoming commissioner with Minister of Works Qiao Lin as deputy; four Shen clansmen were appointed as adjudicators and sent with palace envoys to search the circuits.

sentences.zh: 十一月，初令待制官外，更引朝集使二人，訪以時政得失，遠人疾苦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, beyond the attendance officers, two assembly envoys were first additionally summoned and questioned on the gains and losses of current policy and the hardships of distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, in addition to attendance officers, two assembly envoys were summoned and questioned about policy and the hardships of distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 先是，公主下嫁者，舅姑拜之，婦不答。

translations.literal: Earlier, when princesses married down, parents-in-law bowed to them and the bride did not return the bow.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when a princess married below her rank, her parents-in-law bowed to her while she made no return bow.

sentences.zh: 上命禮官定公主拜見舅、姑及婿之諸父、兄、姊之儀，舅、姑坐受於中堂，諸父、兄、姊立受於東序，如家人禮。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered ritual officers to fix the ceremonies for princesses bowing to parents-in-law and to the husband's various uncles, elder brothers, and elder sisters: parents-in-law seated in the central hall to receive them; uncles, elder brothers, and elder sisters standing in the eastern wing to receive them--like family custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered ritual officers to prescribe how princesses should bow to parents-in-law and to the husband's senior relatives: parents-in-law seated in the central hall, uncles and elder siblings standing in the eastern wing--as in an ordinary household.

sentences.zh: 有縣主將嫁，擇用丁丑。

translations.literal: A county princess was about to marry and had chosen the day dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: A county princess was about to marry on dingchou.

sentences.zh: 是日，上之從父妹卒，命罷之。

translations.literal: That day the emperor's paternal cousin died, and he ordered the wedding canceled.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor's paternal cousin died, and he ordered the wedding canceled.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「供張已備，且殤服不足廢事。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported: 'The supplies are already prepared, and mourning for a child does not require abandoning affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported: 'The preparations are complete, and mourning for a young cousin need not cancel the event.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「爾愛其費，我愛其禮。

translations.literal: '" The emperor said: 'You prize the expense; I prize the ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor said, 'You care about the cost; I care about the ritual.'

sentences.zh: 」卒罷之。

translations.literal: '" In the end he canceled it.
translations.idiomatic: '" He canceled it anyway.

sentences.zh: 至德以來，國家多事，公主、郡、縣主多不以時嫁。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide era the state had many troubles; princesses, commandery princesses, and county princesses mostly did not marry on time.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide era the realm had been in turmoil, and imperial princesses often married late.

sentences.zh: 有華發者，雖居禁中，或十年不見天子。

translations.literal: Some who had gray hair, though dwelling within the palace, might go ten years without seeing the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Some had gone gray in the palace without seeing the emperor for ten years.

sentences.zh: 上始引見諸宗女，尊者致敬，卑者存慰，悉命嫁之。

translations.literal: The emperor first received and saw the various imperial clanswomen; to those senior he paid respect, to those junior he offered comfort--and ordered all to marry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned all the imperial clanswomen: he paid respect to the elders, comforted the younger ones, and ordered every one of them married.

sentences.zh: 所繼小大之物，必經心目。

translations.literal: As for dowries large and small, he personally reviewed every item.
translations.idiomatic: Every dowry, great or small, passed before his eyes.

sentences.zh: 己卯、庚辰二日，嫁岳陽等凡十一縣主。

translations.literal: On the two days jimao and gengchen, eleven county princesses including Yueyang were married.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao and gengchen eleven county princesses, including Yueyang, were married off.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃見韋倫再至，益喜。

translations.literal: Tibet, seeing Wei Lun come again, was all the more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was pleased to see Wei Lun return once more.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛卯朔，倫還，吐蕃遣其相論飲明思等入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month xinmao, Lun returned; Tibet sent its chancellor Lun Yimingsi and others to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month, xinmao, Lun returned; Tibet sent Chancellor Lun Yimingsi and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，冊太子母王氏為淑妃。

translations.literal: That year, the crown prince's mother, Lady Wang, was enfeoffed as Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: That year the crown prince's mother, Lady Wang, was created Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 天下稅戶三百八萬五千七十六，籍後七十六萬八千餘人，稅錢一千八十九萬八千餘緡，谷二百一十五萬七千餘斛。

translations.literal: Taxpaying households under Heaven numbered three million eighty-five thousand seventy-six; persons added to the register afterward seventy-six thousand eight hundred-odd; tax cash one thousand eighty-nine thousand eight hundred-odd strings; grain two million one hundred fifty-seven thousand-odd hu.
translations.idiomatic: Registered tax households nationwide numbered 3,085,076; post-census additions exceeded 768,000 persons; tax revenue exceeded 10.898 million strings of cash; grain exceeded 2.157 million hu.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝下建中二年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Daizong, the Sagaciously Cultured, Filial, and Martial, the second year of Jianzhong (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daizong, the Sagaciously Cultured, Filial, and Martial--the second year of Jianzhong (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元七八一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, corresponding to the year 781 of the Common Era).
translations.idiomatic: xinyou, corresponding to 781 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊辰，成德節度使李寶臣薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day wuchen, Li Baochen, military governor of Chengde, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on wuchen, Li Baochen, military governor of Chengde, died.

sentences.zh: 寶臣欲以軍府傳其子行軍司馬惟岳，以其年少闇弱，豫誅諸將之難制者深州刺史張獻誠等，至有十餘人同日死者。

translations.literal: Baochen wished to pass the army headquarters to his son, Chief of Staff Wei Yue; because the youth was dim and weak, he preemptively executed generals hard to control, including Zhang Xiancheng, prefect of Shenzhou--more than ten men died on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen meant to pass command to his son Wei Yue, chief of staff. Fearing the young man's weakness, he preemptively executed hard-to-control generals including Shenzhou Prefect Zhang Xiancheng--more than ten died on the same day.

sentences.zh: 寶臣召易州刺史張孝忠，孝忠不往，使其弟孝節召之。

translations.literal: Baochen summoned Zhang Xiaozhong, prefect of Yizhou; Xiaozhong did not go, but sent his younger brother Xiaojie to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen summoned Yizhou Prefect Zhang Xiaozhong, who refused to come and sent his brother Xiaojie instead.

sentences.zh: 孝忠使孝節謂寶臣曰：「諸將何罪，連頸受戮！

translations.literal: Xiaozhong had Xiaojie say to Baochen: 'What crime did the generals commit, that they were beheaded one after another!'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong sent Xiaojie to tell Baochen, 'What had those generals done to be slaughtered one after another!'

sentences.zh: 孝忠懼死，不敢往，亦不敢叛，正如公不入朝之意耳。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong fears death and dares not come, yet dares not rebel either--it is just like Your Lordship's intention not to enter court.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong fears death and will not come, yet he will not rebel either--it is the same as Your Lordship's wish not to enter court.'

sentences.zh: 」孝節泣曰：「如此，孝節必死。

translations.literal: '" Xiaojie wept and said: 'If it is thus, Xiaojie will surely die.'
translations.idiomatic: '" Xiaojie wept: 'Then I am as good as dead.'

sentences.zh: 」孝忠曰：「往則並命，我在此，必不敢殺汝。

translations.literal: '" Xiaozhong said: 'If you go we die together; while I am here he surely dares not kill you.'
translations.idiomatic: '" Xiaozhong said, 'If you go we both die--but while I am here he will not dare kill you.'

sentences.zh: 」遂歸，寶臣亦不之罪也。

translations.literal: '" Xiaojie returned, and Baochen did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: '" Xiaojie returned, and Baochen did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使王武俊，位卑而有勇，故寶臣特親愛之，以女妻其子士真，士真復厚結其左右。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun, commander of cavalry and infantry, though low in rank possessed courage; therefore Baochen especially favored him, gave his daughter to Wujun's son Shizhen in marriage, and Shizhen in turn richly bound Baochen's close followers to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun, though low in rank, was bold in battle, so Baochen favored him--giving his daughter to Wujun's son Shizhen and letting Shizhen lavish gifts on Baochen's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 故孝忠、武俊獨得全。

translations.literal: Therefore Xiaozhong and Wujun alone were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiaozhong and Wujun were spared.

sentences.zh: 及薨，孔目官胡震，家僮王它奴勸惟岳匿喪二十餘日，詐為寶臣表，求令惟岳繼襲，上不許。

translations.literal: When he died, Clerk Hu Zhen and house slave Wang Tanu urged Wei Yue to conceal the death for more than twenty days, forge a memorial as from Baochen, and request that Wei Yue succeed; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: After Baochen's death, Clerk Hu Zhen and house slave Wang Tanu urged Wei Yue to conceal the death for more than twenty days, forge a memorial in Baochen's name asking that Wei Yue succeed--and the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 遣給事中汲人班宏往問寶臣疾，且諭之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Supervising Censor Ban Hong of Jiren to inquire after Baochen's illness and also instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Supervising Censor Ban Hong of Jiren to inquire after Baochen's illness and deliver its instructions.

sentences.zh: 惟岳厚賂宏，宏不受，還報。

translations.literal: Wei Yue lavishly bribed Hong, but Hong did not accept and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue tried to bribe Hong lavishly; Hong refused and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 惟岳乃發喪，自為留後，使將佐共奏求旌節，上又不許。

translations.literal: Wei Yue then announced the funeral, made himself acting prefect, and had his staff jointly memorialize requesting the command baton--the emperor again did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue then announced the death, declared himself acting prefect, and had his officers jointly request formal appointment--the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 初，寶臣與李正己、田承嗣、梁崇義相結，期以土地傳之子孫。

translations.literal: At first Baochen allied with Li Zhengji, Tian Chengsi, and Liang Chongyi, agreeing to pass their territories to their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen had allied with Li Zhengji, Tian Chengsi, and Liang Chongyi, pledging to pass their domains to their heirs.

sentences.zh: 故承嗣之死，寶臣力為之請於朝，使以節授田悅；

translations.literal: Therefore at Chengsi's death, Baochen forcefully pleaded for him at court, obtaining the baton for Tian Yue;
translations.idiomatic: When Chengsi died, Baochen had pressed the court to grant the command to Tian Yue;

sentences.zh: 代宗從之。

translations.literal: Daizong consented.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong had agreed.

sentences.zh: 悅初襲位，事朝廷禮甚恭，河東節度使馬燧表其必反，請先為備。

translations.literal: When Yue first succeeded, he served the court with great reverence; Ma Sui, military governor of Hedong, memorialized that he would surely rebel and requested advance preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue first succeeded he was outwardly deferential; Hedong Governor Ma Sui warned that he would rebel and asked for preparations.

sentences.zh: 至是悅屢為惟岳請繼襲，上欲革前弊，不許。

translations.literal: At this Yue repeatedly pleaded for Wei Yue's succession; the emperor wished to reform the old abuse and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yue repeatedly petitioned for Wei Yue's succession, but the emperor sought to end the old abuse and refused.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「惟岳己據父業，不因而命之，必為亂。

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated, saying: 'Wei Yue already holds his father's enterprise; if he is not appointed accordingly, he will surely rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: An adviser warned: 'Wei Yue already controls his father's domain; if you do not appoint him, he will rebel.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「賊本無資以為亂，皆藉我土地，假我位號，以聚其眾耳。

translations.literal: '" The emperor said: 'Rebels originally have no resources for rebellion; they all borrow our territory and borrow our titles to gather their masses--that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor said, 'Rebels have no strength of their own--they borrow our land and titles to gather followers.'

sentences.zh: 曏日因其所欲而命之多矣，而亂益滋。

translations.literal: In former days we appointed them according to their desires many times, yet rebellion only grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: We have indulged their wishes again and again, and rebellion has only worsened.

sentences.zh: 是爵命不足以已亂而適足以長亂也。

translations.literal: Thus noble appointment is not enough to stop rebellion but is exactly enough to prolong it.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments cannot stop rebellion--they only feed it.

sentences.zh: 然則惟岳必為亂，命與不命等耳。

translations.literal: If so, Wei Yue will surely rebel; to appoint or not to appoint is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue will rebel either way--appointment or no appointment.

sentences.zh: 」竟不許。

translations.literal: '" In the end he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: '" He still refused.

sentences.zh: 悅乃與李正己各遣使詣惟岳，潛謀勒兵拒命。

translations.literal: Yue then with Li Zhengji each sent envoys to Wei Yue, secretly plotting to muster troops and defy orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and Li Zhengji each sent envoys to Wei Yue to plot armed defiance.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度副使田庭玠謂悅曰：「爾藉伯父遺業，但謹事朝廷，坐享富貴，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: Tian Tingzhi, deputy military governor of Weibo, said to Yue: 'You rely on your uncle's legacy; if you only reverently serve the court and sit enjoying wealth and rank, would that not be good!'
translations.idiomatic: Tian Tingzhi, deputy governor of Weibo, told Yue, 'You inherited your uncle's domain--why not serve the court faithfully and enjoy your wealth in peace!'

sentences.zh: 奈何無故與恆、鄆共為叛臣！

translations.literal: Why for no reason join Heng and Yun as rebel ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Why join the rebels of Heng and Yun for no reason!

sentences.zh: 爾觀兵興以來，逆亂者誰能保其家乎？

translations.literal: Consider since armies rose--who among those who rebelled has preserved his house?
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, which rebel has kept his house safe?

sentences.zh: 必欲行爾之志，可先殺我，無使我見田氏之族滅也。

translations.literal: If you must carry out your intent, you may first kill me--do not let me see the Tian clan extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: If you must go your own way, kill me first--do not make me watch the Tian clan destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」因稱病臥家。

translations.literal: '" Thereupon he claimed illness and lay at home.
translations.idiomatic: '" He then feigned illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 悅自往謝之，庭玠閉門不內，竟以憂卒。

translations.literal: Yue went in person to apologize; Tingzhi shut his door and would not admit him, and in the end died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yue came in person to apologize; Tingzhi shut him out and eventually died of grief.

sentences.zh: 成德判官邵真聞李惟岳之謀，泣諫曰：「先相公受國厚恩，大夫衰絰之中，遽欲負國，此甚不可。

translations.literal: Shao Zhen, adjutant of Chengde, hearing Li Wei Yue's plot, tearfully remonstrated, saying: 'The late prime minister received the state's deep grace; the Lord, still in mourning garments, suddenly wishes to betray the state--this cannot be done.'
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhen, adjutant of Chengde, learned of Wei Yue's plot and pleaded through tears: 'Your father received the state's great favor; you are still in mourning--how can you turn against the throne?'

sentences.zh: 」勸惟岳執李正己使者送京師，且請討之，曰：「如此，朝廷嘉大夫之忠，則旄節庶幾可得。

translations.literal: '" He urged Wei Yue to seize Li Zhengji's envoy and send him to the capital, and also request a punitive campaign, saying: 'If it is thus, the court will commend the Lord's loyalty, and the command baton may perhaps be obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: '" He urged Wei Yue to arrest Li Zhengji's envoy, send him to the capital, and ask to campaign against him: 'If you do, the court will reward your loyalty and you may yet win the command.'

sentences.zh: 」惟岳然之，使真草奏。

translations.literal: '" Wei Yue agreed and had Zhen draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue agreed and had Zhen draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 長史畢華曰：「先公與二道結好二十餘年，奈何一旦棄之！

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Bi Hua said: 'Your late father allied with the two circuits for more than twenty years--how can you cast that aside in a single day!'
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Bi Hua said: 'Your late father kept faith with the two circuits for over twenty years--how can you abandon that alliance overnight!'

sentences.zh: 且雖執其使，朝廷未必見信。

translations.literal: 'Moreover, even if you seize their envoy, the court may not believe you.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Even if you arrest their envoy, the court may not trust you.'

sentences.zh: 正己忽來襲我，孤軍無援，何以待之！

translations.literal: 'If Zhengji suddenly attacks us, a lone army without reinforcements--how could we withstand him!'
translations.idiomatic: 'If Zhengji strikes without warning, we will stand alone with no aid--how could we survive!'

sentences.zh: 」惟岳又從之。

translations.literal: '" Wei Yue again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue again took his advice.

sentences.zh: 前定州刺史谷從政，惟岳之舅也，有膽略，頗讀書，王武俊等皆敬憚之，為寶臣所忌，從政乃稱病杜門。

translations.literal: Former Dingzhou Prefect Gu Congzheng, Wei Yue's maternal uncle, had courage and stratagem, read widely in books; Wang Wujun and others all respected and feared him; Baochen resented him, and Congzheng feigned illness and shut his doors.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Congzheng, former prefect of Dingzhou and Wei Yue's uncle, was bold and well read; Wang Wujun and others respected and feared him. Resented by Baochen, he claimed illness and withdrew from public life.

sentences.zh: 憔岳亦忌之，不與圖事，日夜獨與胡震、王他奴等計議，多散金帛以悅將士。

translations.literal: Wei Yue also resented him, excluded him from planning; day and night he deliberated alone with Hu Zhen, Wang Tanu, and others, and dispersed much gold and silk to win over the officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue resented him too, kept him out of counsel, and spent his days and nights plotting only with Hu Zhen, Wang Tanu, and the rest, scattering gold and silk to buy the troops' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 從政往見憔岳曰：「今海內無事，自上國來者，皆言天子聰明英武，志欲致太平，深不欲諸侯子孫專地。

translations.literal: Congzheng went to see Wei Yue and said: 'The realm is at peace; those coming from the capital all say the Son of Heaven is wise and valiant, intent on bringing great peace, and deeply unwilling to let feudal lords' heirs hold exclusive domains.'
translations.idiomatic: Congzheng went to Wei Yue and said: 'The empire is quiet. Every envoy from the capital reports that the emperor is wise and resolute, bent on restoring peace, and determined not to let the heirs of regional lords keep their domains to themselves.'

sentences.zh: 爾今首違詔命，天子必遣諸道致討。

translations.literal: 'You now are first to defy the imperial edict; the Son of Heaven is sure to send the various circuits to attack.'
translations.idiomatic: 'You are the first to defy the throne. The emperor will surely send every circuit against you.'

sentences.zh: 將士受賞之際，皆言為大夫盡死。

translations.literal: 'When officers and men receive rewards, they all say they will die for the Lord.'
translations.idiomatic: 'While the rewards are fresh, every soldier swears he will die for you.'

sentences.zh: 苟一戰不勝，各惜其生，誰不離心！

translations.literal: 'If one battle is lost, each will cherish his life--who would not turn away!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Lose one battle and each man will cling to his life--who will not desert you!'

sentences.zh: 大將有權者，乘危伺便，咸思取爾以自為功矣。

translations.literal: 'Great generals with power, seizing crisis and watching for opportunity, will all seek to take you to make their own achievement.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Every powerful commander will wait for your weakness and strike, eager to deliver you up and claim the credit.'

sentences.zh: 且先相公所殺高班大將，殆以百數，撓敗之際，其子弟欲復仇者，庸可數乎！

translations.literal: 'Moreover, the late prime minister killed high-ranking generals--nearly a hundred; at the moment of defeat, can their sons and younger brothers seeking revenge be counted!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Your father executed nearly a hundred senior generals. When you falter, how many of their sons and brothers will come seeking blood!'

sentences.zh: 又，相公與幽州有隙，朱滔兄弟常切齒於我，今天子必以為將。

translations.literal: 'Again, the prime minister had a rift with Youzhou; Zhu Tao and his brothers constantly gnash their teeth at us; today the Son of Heaven is sure to make him a general.'
translations.idiomatic: 'And your father feuded with Youzhou. Zhu Tao and his brothers have long hungered to destroy us. The emperor is certain to appoint Zhu Tao commander.'

sentences.zh: 滔與吾擊析相聞，計其聞命疾驅，若虎狼之得獸也，何以當之！

translations.literal: 'Tao and we are only a knocking-board apart; count on him racing at the command--like a tiger or wolf getting prey--how could we withstand him!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Zhu Tao is close enough to hear our night watches. Once he receives his orders he will come at a gallop like a wolf on prey. How could we stand against him!'

sentences.zh: 昔田承嗣從安、史父子同反，身經百戰，凶悍聞於天下，違詔舉兵，自謂無敵。

translations.literal: 'Formerly Tian Chengsi followed An and Shi, father and son, in rebellion together; he personally endured a hundred battles, and his ferocity was known throughout the realm; defying the edict and raising troops, he deemed himself invincible.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Tian Chengsi once rebelled with An Lushan and Shi Siming, fought a hundred battles, and was feared across the empire. When he defied the throne he thought himself invincible.'

sentences.zh: 及盧子期就擒，吳希光歸國，承嗣指天垂泣，身無所措。

translations.literal: 'When Lu Ziqi was captured and Wu Xiguang returned to the state, Chengsi pointed to heaven and wept--he had nowhere to turn.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When Lu Ziqi was taken and Wu Xiguang surrendered, Chengsi wept to heaven, utterly at a loss.'

sentences.zh: 賴先相公按兵不進，且為之祈請，先帝寬仁，赦而不誅，不然，田氏豈有種乎！

translations.literal: 'Only because the late prime minister held his army back and did not advance, and also pleaded on his behalf, did the late emperor, in his clemency, pardon and not execute him--otherwise, would the Tian line have any descendants!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Only because your father held his troops back and pleaded for mercy did the late emperor spare Chengsi. Otherwise the Tian clan would have been wiped out.'

sentences.zh: 況爾生長富貴，齒發尚少，不更艱危，乃信左右之言，欲效承嗣所為乎！

translations.literal: 'Moreover, you were raised in wealth and honor, your teeth and hair still young, untried in hardship--will you trust the words of those beside you and wish to imitate what Chengsi did!'
translations.idiomatic: 'You were bred in luxury, still young and untested. Will you heed flatterers and copy Chengsi's folly!'

sentences.zh: 為爾之計，不若辭謝將佐，使惟誠攝領軍府，身自入朝，乞留宿衛，因言惟誠且令攝事。

translations.literal: 'For your plan, better to decline before your officers, have Wei Cheng temporarily administer the army headquarters, go yourself to court, ask to remain in palace guard service, and meanwhile say Wei Cheng is to handle affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: 'My counsel: step aside before your staff, let Wei Cheng govern the headquarters in your stead, go to court yourself, ask to serve in the palace guard, and say Wei Cheng will manage affairs meanwhile.'

sentences.zh: 恩命決於聖志，上必悅爾忠義，縱無大位，不失榮祿，永無憂矣。

translations.literal: 'Favor and appointment depend on the sage's will; the emperor will surely delight in your loyalty and righteousness; even without a great post, you will not lose honor and stipend, and will never know worry.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The throne decides your fate. The emperor will honor your loyalty. You may not keep the highest rank, but you will keep your honors and live without fear.'

sentences.zh: 不然，大禍將至，悔之何及。

translations.literal: 'Otherwise, great calamity will come--what use to regret when it is too late.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Otherwise disaster is coming, and regret will come too late.'

sentences.zh: 吾亦知爾素疏忌我，顧以舅甥之情，事急，不得不言耳！

translations.literal: 'I also know you have long kept distant and resented me; but for uncle-nephew affection, with affairs urgent, I cannot but speak!'
translations.idiomatic: 'I know you have always distrusted me. But we are kin, and the crisis leaves me no choice but to speak plainly!'

sentences.zh: 」惟岳及左右見其言切，益惡之。

translations.literal: '" Wei Yue and those beside him, seeing his words cutting, hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue and his confidants, stung by his blunt counsel, hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 從政乃復歸，杜門稱病。

translations.literal: Congzheng then returned home and shut his doors, claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: Congzheng went home again, shut his doors, and pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 惟誠者，惟岳之庶兄也，謙厚好書，得眾心，其母妹為李正己子婦。

translations.literal: Wei Cheng was Wei Yue's elder half-brother by a concubine, modest and generous, fond of books, and had won men's hearts; his younger sister by the same mother was the daughter-in-law of Li Zhengji's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cheng, Wei Yue's elder half-brother, was modest, bookish, and beloved by the troops. His younger sister by the same mother had married Li Zhengji's son.

sentences.zh: 是日，惟岳送惟誠於正己，正己使復姓張，遂仕淄青。

translations.literal: That day Wei Yue sent Wei Cheng to Zhengji; Zhengji had him resume the surname Zhang, and he entered service in Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Wei Yue sent Wei Cheng to Zhengji, who restored his original surname Zhang and put him in service at Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 惟岳遣王它奴詣從政家，察其起居，從政飲藥而卒；

translations.literal: Wei Yue sent Wang Tanu to Congzheng's house to observe his daily life; Congzheng drank poison and died;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue sent Wang Tanu to watch Congzheng at home. Congzheng took poison and died;

sentences.zh: 且死，曰：「吾不憚死，哀張氏今族滅矣！

translations.literal: As he was dying he said: 'I do not fear death; I grieve that the Zhang clan is now to be exterminated!'
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he said: 'I do not fear death. I mourn that the Zhang clan is about to be destroyed!'

sentences.zh: 劉文喜之死也，李正己、田悅等皆不自安；

translations.literal: At Liu Wenxi's death, Li Zhengji, Tian Yue, and others were all ill at ease;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wenxi was executed, Li Zhengji, Tian Yue, and the others were shaken;

sentences.zh: 劉晏死，正己等益懼，相謂曰：「我輩罪惡，豈得與劉晏比乎！

translations.literal: When Liu Yan died, Zhengji and the others grew all the more fearful and said to one another: 'Our crimes--how could we compare with Liu Yan!'
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan was killed, Zhengji and the rest grew still more afraid. They said to one another: 'Our crimes are far worse than Liu Yan's--how can we expect mercy!'

sentences.zh: 」會汴州城隘，廣之，東方人訛言：「上欲東封，故城汴州。

translations.literal: '" It happened that Bianzhou's walls were cramped and were being expanded; people in the east spread a false rumor: 'The emperor wishes to perform the eastern feng and shan rites, and therefore is fortifying Bianzhou.'
translations.idiomatic: '" About then Bianzhou's walls were being enlarged because they had grown too cramped. In the east a rumor spread: 'The emperor means to perform the eastern feng and shan rites, and is fortifying Bianzhou for that purpose.'

sentences.zh: 」正己懼，發兵萬人屯曹州。

translations.literal: '" Zhengji feared this and dispatched ten thousand troops to garrison at Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Zhengji mobilized ten thousand men and encamped at Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 田悅亦完聚為備，與梁崇義、李惟岳遙相應助，河南士民騷然驚駭。

translations.literal: Tian Yue also fortified and gathered provisions in preparation; with Liang Chongyi and Li Wei Yue he responded and aided from afar; the people and gentry of Henan were thrown into alarm and panic.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue also gathered stores and made ready for war. He, Liang Chongyi, and Li Wei Yue coordinated from afar, and the people of Henan were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 永平軍舊領汴、宋、滑、亳、陳、穎、泗七州，丙子，分宋、亳、穎別為節度使，以宋州刺史劉洽為之；

translations.literal: The Yongping Army formerly controlled the seven prefectures of Bian, Song, Hua, Bo, Chen, Ying, and Si; on the day bingzi, Song, Bo, and Ying were separated out as a new military commission, with Songzhou Prefect Liu Qia appointed to it;
translations.idiomatic: The Yongping Army had once governed Bian, Song, Hua, Bo, Chen, Ying, and Si--seven prefectures. On the day bingzi, Song, Bo, and Ying were split off into a separate command, with Liu Qia, prefect of Song, as its governor;

sentences.zh: 以泗州隸淮南；

translations.literal: Si Prefecture was placed under Huainan;
translations.idiomatic: Si Prefecture was transferred to Huainan;

sentences.zh: 又以東都留守路嗣恭為懷、鄭、汝、陝四州、河陽三城節度使。

translations.literal: Lu Sigong, Eastern Capital garrison commander, was made military governor of Huai, Zheng, Ru, and Shan--four prefectures--and the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sigong, garrison commander of the Eastern Capital, was made military governor of Huai, Zheng, Ru, and Shan and of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 旬日，又以永平節度使李勉都統洽、嗣恭二道，仍割鄭州隸之，選嘗為將者為諸州刺史，以備正己等。

translations.literal: Within ten days, Yongping military governor Li Mian was made overall commander of Qia's and Sigong's two circuits; Zheng Prefecture was still cut off and placed under him; men who had once served as generals were chosen as prefects of the various prefectures, to guard against Zhengji and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Li Mian, governor of Yongping, was placed in overall command of Qia's and Sigong's circuits. Zheng Prefecture was detached and assigned to him, and veteran generals were appointed prefects throughout the region to guard against Zhengji and his allies.

sentences.zh: 初，高力士有養女嫠居東京，頗能言宮中事，女官李真一意其為沈太后，詣使者具言其狀。

translations.literal: At first, Gao Lishi had an adopted daughter, a widow living in the Eastern Capital, who could speak rather well of palace affairs; the female official Li Zhenyi supposed her to be Empress Dowager Shen and went to the envoy and fully described her condition.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Lishi had an adopted daughter, a widow in the Eastern Capital, who knew much of palace life. The palace woman Li Zhenyi took her for Empress Dowager Shen and reported the matter in full to the imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，驚喜。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and was astonished and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard the report and was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 時沈氏故老已盡，無識太后者，上遣宦官、宮人征驗視之，年狀頗同，宦官、宮人不審識太后，皆言是。

translations.literal: At the time the old retainers of the Shen clan were all gone; there was no one who knew the empress dowager; the emperor sent eunuchs and palace women to summon and verify her; her age and appearance matched rather closely; the eunuchs and palace women did not truly know the empress dowager--all said she was.
translations.idiomatic: By then every elder who had known the Shen clan was dead. With no one left who could recognize the empress dowager, the emperor sent eunuchs and palace women to examine her. Her age and appearance were close enough, and since none of them had ever known the real dowager, all declared that she was.

sentences.zh: 高氏辭稱實非太后，驗視者益疑之，強迎入居上陽宮。

translations.literal: Lady Gao protested that she was truly not the empress dowager; the investigators grew all the more suspicious and forcibly welcomed her in to dwell at Shangyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao insisted she was not the empress dowager, but the investigators only grew more suspicious and forcibly installed her at Shangyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 上發宮女百餘人，繼乘輿御物就上陽宮供奉。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched more than a hundred palace women, followed by imperial carriage goods, to Shangyang Palace to serve her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent more than a hundred palace women, then imperial carriage goods, to Shangyang Palace to attend her.

sentences.zh: 左右誘諭百方，高氏心動，乃自言是。

translations.literal: Those beside her tempted and persuaded in every way; Lady Gao's heart moved, and she then declared herself to be.
translations.idiomatic: Her attendants coaxed her from every angle until she wavered and at last confessed that she was the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 驗視者走馬入奏，上大喜。

translations.literal: The investigators raced their horses to enter and report; the emperor was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: The investigators galloped back to report, and the emperor was elated.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，上以偶日御殿，群臣皆入賀。
