translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinmao, because it was an auspicious day the emperor held court; all the ministers entered to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day xinmao, the emperor held court on an auspicious day and the whole ministry came to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 詔有司草儀奉迎。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to draft rites for welcoming her.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the proper offices to draft the rites for her formal welcome.

sentences.zh: 高氏弟承悅在長安，恐不言，久獲罪，遽自言本末。

translations.literal: Lady Gao's younger brother Chengyue was in Chang'an; fearing that if he did not speak he would long bear guilt, he suddenly revealed the whole story.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao's brother Chengyue was in Chang'an. Afraid that silence would eventually ruin him, he suddenly told the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 上命力士養孫樊景超往覆視，景超見高氏居內殿，以太后自處，左右侍衛甚嚴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Lishi's adopted grandson Fan Jingchao to go and re-examine; Jingchao saw Lady Gao dwelling in the inner hall, comporting herself as empress dowager, with attendants guarding her very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Lishi's adopted grandson Fan Jingchao to investigate again. Jingchao found Lady Gao in the inner hall, playing the empress dowager, surrounded by a strict guard.

sentences.zh: 景超謂高氏曰：「姑何自置身於俎上！

translations.literal: Jingchao said to Lady Gao: 'Aunt, why do you place yourself on the chopping block!'
translations.idiomatic: Jingchao said to Lady Gao: 'Aunt, why do you put your neck on the block!'

sentences.zh: 」左右叱景超使下，景超抗聲曰：「有詔，太后詐偽，左右可下。

translations.literal: '" Those beside her rebuked Jingchao and told him to withdraw; Jingchao raised his voice and said: 'There is an edict: the empress dowager is fraudulent; attendants may withdraw.'
translations.idiomatic: '" Her attendants ordered Jingchao down. He shouted: 'By imperial edict: the empress dowager is an impostor. Attendants, withdraw.'

sentences.zh: 」左右皆下殿。

translations.literal: '" All those beside her withdrew from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: They all left the hall.

sentences.zh: 高氏乃曰：「吾為人所強，非己出也。

translations.literal: Lady Gao then said: 'I was compelled by others; it was not my own intention.'
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao then said: 'Others forced me into this. It was never my own wish.'

sentences.zh: 」以牛車載還其家。

translations.literal: '" She was carried back to her home in an ox cart.
translations.idiomatic: She was sent home in an ox cart.

sentences.zh: 上恐後人不復敢言太后，皆不之罪，曰：「吾寧受百欺，庶幾得之。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing that afterward no one would dare speak of the empress dowager again, punished none of them, saying: 'I would rather be deceived a hundred times, if only I might find her.'
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that no one would ever dare report the empress dowager again, the emperor punished no one and said: 'I would rather be fooled a hundred times if it might bring me to her at last.'

sentences.zh: 」自是四方稱得太后者數四，皆非是，而真太后竟不知所之。

translations.literal: '" From then on, four times in all from the four directions came claims of having found the empress dowager--none was genuine--and the true empress dowager's whereabouts were never known.
translations.idiomatic: '" After that, four more claimants from across the empire were hailed as the empress dowager, and all proved false. The real empress dowager was never found.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞盧杞，弈之子也，貌醜，色如藍，有口辯。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Lu Qi was the son of Lu Yi; his appearance was ugly, his complexion like indigo, and he had eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, vice censor-in-chief and son of Lu Yi, was ugly, with a bluish cast to his face, but he was a fluent speaker.

sentences.zh: 上悅之，丁未，擢為大夫，領京畿觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with him; on the day dingwei, he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and given charge as Metropolitan Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took to him. On the day dingwei he was promoted to censor-in-chief and made metropolitan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀每見賓客，姬妾不離側。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, whenever he received guests, kept his concubines at his side without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Guo Ziyi received guests, his concubines never left his side.

sentences.zh: 杞嘗往問疾，子儀悉屏侍妾，獨隱-{几}-待之。

translations.literal: Qi once went to inquire after his health; Ziyi dismissed all his attendant concubines and waited for him alone, reclining at his armrest.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi once came to inquire after his health, Ziyi dismissed every concubine and received him alone, seated at his armrest.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，子儀曰：「杞貌陋而心險，婦人輩見之必笑，他日杞得志，吾族無類矣！

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Ziyi said: 'Qi's appearance is homely and his heart treacherous; the women would surely laugh when they saw him; when Qi one day gains his aim, my clan will be wiped out!'
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Ziyi said: 'Qi is ugly and treacherous. The women would laugh at him, and when Qi rises to power my whole clan will be destroyed!'

sentences.zh: 楊炎既殺劉晏，朝野側目，李正己累表請晏罪，譏斥朝廷。

translations.literal: Yang Yan, having killed Liu Yan, drew sidelong glances from court and country; Li Zhengji repeatedly memorialized requesting Yan's crimes be punished, ridiculing and denouncing the court.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yan had Liu Yan executed, court and country watched him with fear. Li Zhengji repeatedly memorialized demanding Yan's punishment and mocked the throne.

sentences.zh: 炎懼，遣腹心分詣諸道，以宣慰為名，實使之密諭節度使云：「晏昔附奸邪，請立獨孤后，上自惡而殺之。

translations.literal: Yan feared this and sent trusted men separately to the various circuits, under the name of consolation envoy, actually having them secretly tell the military governors: 'Yan formerly attached himself to wicked faction, sought to establish Empress Dugu; the emperor himself hated this and had him killed.'
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Yan sent trusted agents to every circuit under the guise of consolation. Secretly he had them tell each governor: 'Liu Yan once joined wicked factions and sought to make Empress Dugu regent. The emperor himself loathed him and ordered his death.'

sentences.zh: 」上聞而惡之，由是有誅炎之志，隱而未發。

translations.literal: '" The emperor heard and was displeased; from this he had the will to execute Yan, but concealed it and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he was disgusted, and from then on resolved to destroy Yan, though he kept the intent hidden.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遷炎中書侍郎，擢盧杞為門下侍郎，並同平章事，不專任炎矣。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Yan was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat; Lu Qi was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery; both were appointed Junior Chancellors of equal rank--Yan was no longer solely entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, Yan was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and Lu Qi was promoted to vice director of the chancellery. Both became junior chancellors, and Yan was no longer left in sole charge.

sentences.zh: 杞蕞陋，無文學，炎輕之，多托疾不與會食；

translations.literal: Qi was short and homely, without literary accomplishment; Yan slighted him and often pleaded illness and did not join him for meals;
translations.idiomatic: Qi was short, homely, and unlearned. Yan looked down on him and often feigned illness to avoid dining with him;

sentences.zh: 杞亦恨之。

translations.literal: Qi also resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi hated him in return.

sentences.zh: 杞陰狡，欲起勢立威，小不附者必欲置之死地，引太常博士裴延齡為集賢殿直學士，親任之。

translations.literal: Qi was secretly cunning; he wished to raise his power and establish authority; anyone slightly not attached to him he was sure to seek to destroy; he brought in Doctor of the Grand Shrine Pei Yanling as a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and trusted him personally.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was secretly ruthless and sought power through fear. Anyone who slighted him he tried to destroy. He brought in Pei Yanling, doctor of the Grand Shrine, as a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and relied on him closely.

sentences.zh: 丙午，更汴宋軍名曰宣武。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, the Bian-Song army was renamed Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu the Bian-Song army was renamed the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 振武節度使彭令芳苛虐，監軍劉惠光貪婪。

translations.literal: Zhenwu military governor Peng Lingfang was harsh and cruel; army supervisor Liu Huiguang was greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Lingfang, military governor of Zhenwu, was brutal; Liu Huiguang, the army supervisor, was corrupt.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，軍士共殺之。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the soldiers jointly killed them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao the soldiers killed them both.

sentences.zh: 發京西防秋兵萬二千人戍關東。

translations.literal: Twelve thousand autumn-defense troops from the capital region were dispatched to garrison Guandong.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve thousand autumn-defense troops from the capital region were sent to garrison Guandong.

sentences.zh: 上御望春樓宴勞將士，神策將士獨不飲，上使詰之，其將楊惠元對曰：「臣等發奉天，軍帥張巨濟戒之曰：『此行大建功名，凱旋之日，相與為歡。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted Wangchun Tower to feast and reward the troops; the Shence troops alone did not drink; the emperor had them questioned; their general Yang Huiyuan replied: 'We set out from Fengtian; our army commander Zhang Juji admonished us, saying: "On this campaign you will win great merit; on the day of triumphant return, we shall rejoice together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted the troops at Wangchun Tower. Only the Shence soldiers refused wine. When questioned, their commander Yang Huiyuan answered: 'We marched from Fengtian. Our commander Zhang Juji warned us: "This campaign is for glory. When we return in triumph we shall feast together.

sentences.zh: 苟未捷，勿飲酒。

translations.literal: If victory is not yet won, do not drink wine."'
translations.idiomatic: Until victory is won, do not drink."'

sentences.zh: 』故不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: ' Therefore we dare not obey the edict to drink.'
translations.idiomatic: ' So we dare not accept your invitation to drink.'

sentences.zh: 」及行，有司緣道設酒食，獨惠元所部瓶罌不發。

translations.literal: '" When they marched, the relevant offices set out wine and food along the route; only Huiyuan's division did not break open their jars and bottles.
translations.idiomatic: On the march, officials offered wine along the road, but only Huiyuan's unit kept their jars sealed.

sentences.zh: 上深歎美，賜書勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply sighed in admiration and bestowed a letter commending him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration and sent a letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 惠元，平州人也。

translations.literal: Huiyuan was a man of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyuan was from Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，置殷州於郾城。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yin Prefecture was established at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yin Prefecture was established at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以汾州刺史王翃為振武軍使、鎮北、綏、銀等州留後。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Wang Hong, prefect of Fenzhou, was made commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and acting governor of Zhenbei, Sui, Yin, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Wang Hong, prefect of Fen, was made commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and acting governor of Zhenbei, Sui, Yin, and the other northern prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遣殿中少監崔漢衡使於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Palace aide Cui Hanheng was sent as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Palace aide Cui Hanheng was dispatched as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 梁崇義雖與李正己等連結，兵勢寡弱，禮數最恭。

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi, though allied with Li Zhengji and the others, had few troops and weak strength; in ritual and deference he was most respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi was allied with Li Zhengji and the others, but his forces were weak and he was the most deferential of them all.

sentences.zh: 或勸其入朝，崇義曰：「來公有大功於國，上元中為閹宦所讒，遷延稽命，及代宗嗣位，不俟駕入朝，猶不免族誅。

translations.literal: Someone urged him to enter court; Chongyi said: 'Lord Lai had great merit for the state; in the Shangyuan era he was slandered by eunuchs, delayed and put off answering the summons; when Emperor Daizong succeeded to the throne, he entered court without waiting for the imperial progress--and still could not escape execution of his entire clan.'
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to go to court, Chongyi said: 'Lord Lai served the state with great merit. In the Shangyuan era eunuchs slandered him and he delayed answering the summons. Even after Emperor Daizong succeeded, though Lai entered court without waiting for the imperial progress, his whole clan was still executed.'

sentences.zh: 吾歲久釁積，何可往也！

translations.literal: 'I have accumulated grievances for years--how could I go!'
translations.idiomatic: 'I have old grievances of my own. How could I dare go!'

sentences.zh: 」淮寧節度使李希烈屢請討之，崇義懼，益修武備。

translations.literal: '" Huaining military governor Li Xilie repeatedly requested permission to campaign against him; Chongyi feared this and all the more strengthened his military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Huaining governor Li Xilie repeatedly asked to campaign against him. Chongyi was afraid and redoubled his defenses.

sentences.zh: 流人郭昔告崇義為變，崇義聞之，請罪，上為之杖昔，遠流之；

translations.literal: Exile Guo Xi reported that Chongyi was plotting rebellion; Chongyi heard and begged forgiveness; the emperor had Xi beaten on his account and exiled him far away;
translations.idiomatic: An exile named Guo Xi accused Chongyi of plotting rebellion. Chongyi submitted a plea of guilt, and the emperor had Guo beaten and banished far away;

sentences.zh: 使金部員外郎李舟詣襄州諭旨以安之。

translations.literal: He sent Secretary of the Ministry of Revenue Li Zhou to Xiangzhou to convey the imperial intent and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Zhou of the Ministry of Revenue to Xiangzhou to reassure him with the imperial message.

sentences.zh: 舟嘗奉使詣劉文喜，為陳禍福，文喜囚之，會帳下殺文喜以降，諸道跋扈者聞之，謂舟能覆城殺將。

translations.literal: Zhou had once been sent as envoy to Liu Wenxi; he set forth fortune and calamity; Wenxi imprisoned him; it happened that men under Wenxi killed Wenxi and surrendered; overbearing men in the various circuits heard of this and said Zhou could overturn a city and kill a general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had once been sent to Liu Wenxi to warn him of the consequences of rebellion. Wenxi imprisoned him, but his own men killed Wenxi and surrendered. Overbearing governors everywhere decided that Zhou could topple a fortress and kill its commander.

sentences.zh: 至襄州，崇義惡之。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangzhou, Chongyi hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou reached Xiangzhou, Chongyi loathed him.

sentences.zh: 舟又勸崇義入朝，言頗切直，崇義益不悅。

translations.literal: Zhou again urged Chongyi to enter court; his words were rather blunt and direct; Chongyi grew all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou again urged Chongyi to go to court, this time in blunt terms, and Chongyi liked him even less.

sentences.zh: 及遣使宣慰諸道，舟復指襄州，崇義拒境不內，上言「軍中疑懼，請易以它使。

translations.literal: When envoys were dispatched to console the various circuits, Zhou again headed for Xiangzhou; Chongyi barred the border and would not admit him, memorializing: 'The army is suspicious and fearful; please replace him with another envoy.'
translations.idiomatic: When consolation envoys were sent to the circuits, Zhou was again directed toward Xiangzhou. Chongyi closed the border and refused him entry, memorializing: 'The army is uneasy. Send another envoy.'

sentences.zh: 」時兩河諸鎮方猜阻，上欲示恩信以安之，夏，四月，庚寅，加崇義同平章事，妻子悉加封賞，賜以鐵券；

translations.literal: '" At the time the garrison lords of the two He regions were mutually suspicious and obstructive; the emperor wished to show favor and trust to reassure them; in summer, the fourth month, on the day gengyin, Chongyi was given the title of Junior Chancellor of equal rank; his wife and children were all ennobled and rewarded; he was granted an iron certificate;
translations.idiomatic: '" The governors of the two He regions were then mutually suspicious. To reassure them the emperor, in summer, the fourth month, on the day gengyin, made Chongyi a junior chancellor, ennobled his wife and children, and granted him an iron certificate;

sentences.zh: 遣御史張著繼手詔征之，仍以其裨將藺杲為鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Zhu was sent with a handwritten edict summoning him; his subordinate general Lin Gao was still made prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Censor Zhang Zhu with a handwritten edict summoning Chongyi to court, while appointing his subordinate Lin Gao prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，以軍興，增商稅為什一。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingyin, because of military mobilization, the merchant tax was raised to one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day bingyin, because of the war mobilization the merchant tax was raised to ten percent.

sentences.zh: 田悅卒與李正己、李惟岳定計，連兵拒命，遣兵馬使孟祐將步騎五千北助惟岳。

translations.literal: Tian Yue finally joined Li Zhengji and Li Wei Yue in a fixed plan; they linked armies to defy orders and sent troop-and-horse commissioner Meng You with five thousand infantry and cavalry north to aid Wei Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue at last joined Li Zhengji and Li Wei Yue in a firm plan to resist the throne. They combined forces and sent troop commissioner Meng You north with five thousand infantry and cavalry to aid Wei Yue.

sentences.zh: 薛嵩之死也，田承嗣盜據洺、相二州，朝廷獨得邢、磁二州及臨洺縣。

translations.literal: At Xue Song's death, Tian Chengsi seized by force the two prefectures of Ming and Xiang; the court obtained only Xing and Ci--two prefectures--and Linming County.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Song died, Tian Chengsi seized Ming and Xiang by force, leaving the court with only Xing, Ci, and Linming County.

sentences.zh: 悅欲阻山為境，曰：「邢、磁如兩眼，在吾腹中，不可不取。

translations.literal: Yue wished to take the mountains as his border and said: 'Xing and Ci are like two eyes in my belly--they cannot go untaken.'
translations.idiomatic: Yue wanted the mountains as his frontier and said: 'Xing and Ci are like two eyes in my belly. I must take them.'

sentences.zh: 」乃遣兵馬使康愔將八千人圍邢州，別將楊朝光將五千人柵於邯鄲西北，以斷昭義救兵，悅自將兵數萬圍臨洺。

translations.literal: '" He then sent troop-and-horse commissioner Kang Yin with eight thousand men to besiege Xingzhou; deputy general Yang Chaoguang with five thousand men encamped northwest of Handan to cut off Zhaoyi's relief troops; Yue personally led tens of thousands to besiege Linming.
translations.idiomatic: '" He sent troop commissioner Kang Yin with eight thousand men to besiege Xing, stationed Yang Chaoguang with five thousand northwest of Handan to block Zhaoyi's relief, and personally led tens of thousands to besiege Linming.

sentences.zh: 邢州刺史李共、臨洺將張伾堅壁拒守。

translations.literal: Li Gong, prefect of Xingzhou, and Zhang Pi, general of Linming, held their walls firmly and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gong, prefect of Xingzhou, and Zhang Pi, commander of Linming, held their walls and resisted stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 貝州刺史邢曹俊，田承嗣舊將也，老而有謀，悅寵信牙官扈崿而疏之。

translations.literal: Xing Caojun, prefect of Beizhou, was an old officer of Tian Chengsi; aged but resourceful, Yue favored and trusted his personal guard officer Hu E and kept Caojun at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Caojun, prefect of Beizhou, was a veteran officer of Tian Chengsi. Though aged, he was shrewd, but Yue favored his personal guard officer Hu E and kept Caojun at a distance.

sentences.zh: 及攻臨洺，召曹俊問計。

translations.literal: When he attacked Linming, he summoned Caojun to ask his plan.
translations.idiomatic: When he attacked Linming, he summoned Caojun to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 曹俊曰：「兵法十圍五攻；

translations.literal: Caojun said: "In the art of war, tenfold strength besieges and fivefold attacks;
translations.idiomatic: Caojun said, 'In the art of war, tenfold strength besieges and fivefold strength attacks;

sentences.zh: 尚書以逆犯順，勢更不侔。

translations.literal: the Minister is rebelling against obedience—your power is even less comparable.
translations.idiomatic: you, Minister, are rebelling against the throne—your power is even less than that.

sentences.zh: 今頓兵堅城之下，糧竭卒盡，自亡之道也。

translations.literal: Now you halt your army beneath a strong city; when grain is exhausted and soldiers spent, that is the way to destroy yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Now you halt your army beneath a strong city. When grain runs out and your soldiers are spent, that is the path to your own destruction.

sentences.zh: 不若置萬兵於崞口以遏西師，則河北二十四州皆為尚書有矣。

translations.literal: Better to post ten thousand troops at Guokou to block the western army—then all twenty-four prefectures of Hebei will be the Minister's.
translations.idiomatic: Better to post ten thousand troops at Guokou to block the western army—then all twenty-four prefectures of Hebei will be yours.'

sentences.zh: 」諸將惡其異己，共毀之，悅不用其策。

translations.literal: The generals resented that he differed from them and together slandered him; Yue did not use his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The generals resented his dissent and together slandered him; Yue did not adopt his plan.

translations.idiomatic: Category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance.
